dimensions.label: AI data centers
dimensions.question: Should America build AI data centers as fast as possible, or slow down until electric bills, water and communities are protected?

dimensions.label: AI risk and control
dimensions.question: How dangerous is advanced AI, and how hard should the government regulate the companies building it?

dimensions.label: Big Tech regulation
dimensions.question: Should Washington rein in the big technology companies (kids safety, privacy, antitrust, Section 230), or leave them mostly alone?

dimensions.label: State AI laws
dimensions.question: Should states be allowed to pass their own AI laws, or should one national rule block them?

dimensions.label: China and AI chips
dimensions.question: Should the U.S. keep its most advanced AI chips away from China, or sell more of them abroad?

votes.title: Should states keep the right to regulate AI?
votes.plain: The House version of the 2025 Republican tax-and-spending law (H.R. 1) contained a 10-year ban on states enforcing their own AI laws. On July 1, 2025 the Senate voted on Sen. Marsha Blackburn's amendment to strip that ban out. It passed 99 to 1 after a compromise between Blackburn and Sen. Ted Cruz collapsed overnight. Because almost everyone voted yes, including Cruz, this vote alone does not tell you who supports a national rule; the positions on this site come from what members said and sponsored.
votes.yea_means: Strip the ban: states keep their power to regulate AI
votes.nay_means: Keep the 10-year ban on state AI laws

votes.title: House passes the budget bill that carried the 10-year ban on state AI laws
votes.plain: On May 22, 2025 the House passed H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, 215 to 214. Buried inside was a 10-year moratorium on state and local AI laws. This was a vote on a giant bill, so it says little about any one member's AI views. Several Republicans, including Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, later said they did not know the AI provision was in it and would have opposed it. The Senate removed the provision before the bill became law.
votes.yea_means: Pass the budget bill (with the state AI law ban inside)

votes.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act: a federal crime to post AI sexual deepfakes without consent
votes.plain: The TAKE IT DOWN Act makes it a federal crime to publish real or AI-generated sexual images of a person without consent and forces platforms to remove them within 48 hours of a request. The House passed it 409 to 2 on April 28, 2025 and President Trump signed it in May 2025. The two no votes were Reps. Thomas Massie and Eric Burlison, who cited free speech and government overreach concerns.

votes.title: KIDS Act: the Republican kids-online-safety package, with AI chatbot rules
votes.plain: On June 29, 2026 the House passed the KIDS Act 267 to 117. The Republican-led package bundled kids' online safety rules, app store age checks and new rules for AI chatbots that talk to minors. Most Democrats voted no, arguing it was a weaker substitute for the Senate's Kids Online Safety Act and gave tech companies too much cover; a yes vote here reads as support for the GOP approach, not necessarily as pro or anti regulation.
votes.yea_means: Pass the House GOP kids-safety and chatbot package
votes.nay_means: Reject it (most Democrats wanted the stronger Senate KOSA)

votes.title: Remote Access Security Act: close the cloud loophole in AI chip export controls
votes.plain: Export controls stop China from buying America's most advanced AI chips, but Chinese firms could still rent the same chips remotely through the cloud. This bill lets the Commerce Department control that remote access too. The House passed it 369 to 22 on January 12, 2026.
votes.yea_means: Tighten controls on Chinese access to U.S. AI chips

votes.title: Repeal the consumer watchdog's oversight of Big Tech payment apps
votes.plain: In late 2024 the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau finalized a rule letting it supervise large digital payment apps (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Venmo, Cash App) the way it supervises banks. On March 5, 2025 the Senate voted 51 to 47, along party lines, to repeal that rule; the House agreed 219 to 211 in April and the repeal became law. A yes vote was a vote for lighter oversight of Big Tech's financial products.
votes.yea_means: Repeal the oversight rule (lighter touch on Big Tech)
votes.nay_means: Keep the watchdog's oversight of payment apps

votes.title: House vote to repeal the consumer watchdog's oversight of Big Tech payment apps
votes.plain: The House companion vote on April 9, 2025 (219 to 211) to the Senate repeal of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's rule supervising large digital payment apps. See the Senate vote above for the background.
votes.yea_means: Repeal the oversight rule (lighter touch on Big Tech)
votes.nay_means: Keep the watchdog's oversight of payment apps

votes.title: Kids Online Safety Act passes the Senate (2024)
votes.plain: The Kids Online Safety Act would give social media companies a legal duty of care to protect children from bullying, sexual exploitation and content that promotes self-harm, and let parents turn off addictive features. The Senate passed it 91 to 3 on July 30, 2024 (Sens. Wyden, Paul and Lee voted no, citing free-speech and censorship concerns). The House never took it up that year, and the fight over a House version continued into 2026.
votes.yea_means: Pass kids' online safety rules for social media

votes.title: Force TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a U.S. ban
votes.plain: On March 13, 2024 the House voted 352 to 65 to require ByteDance to sell TikTok or see the app banned in the United States. A version of the measure became law the following month. The no votes came from both parties: progressives worried about free speech and some Republicans who opposed the precedent of banning an app.
votes.yea_means: Force a sale or ban of TikTok
votes.nay_means: Oppose the forced sale or ban

votes.title: Stop the government from buying Americans' data from brokers
votes.plain: The Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act would stop law enforcement and intelligence agencies from buying Americans' location and browsing data from data brokers without a warrant. The House passed it 219 to 199 on April 17, 2024 with an unusual coalition of privacy-minded Republicans and Democrats; the Senate never voted on it.
votes.yea_means: Ban warrantless government purchases of personal data

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: As the DFL nominee for governor she says data centers raise electric rates and hurt the environment, wants local control, strong state standards, full cost recovery from developers and an end to secret NDAs. She has not endorsed a moratorium and did not answer directly when asked about local moratoria.

evidence.title: KFGO radio interview: Klobuchar on data centers as candidate for governor
evidence.quote: Cause people's rates to go up, they have hurt the environment, and that just can't keep happening. So my answer to this is number one, local control.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words: data centers are a rate and environmental problem, and locals should decide; she also said NDAs with officials should not be happening.

evidence.title: West Central Tribune candidate survey on data centers
evidence.quote: If Minnesotans don't want a data center in their community, I don't want it there either.
evidence.what_it_shows: She would require projects to cover 100 percent of energy and grid costs, disclose power and water demand before local approval, and report annually; she attacked her opponent for blocking an NDA ban.

evidence.title: Minnesota Reformer questionnaire: spokesman on Klobuchar's data center position
evidence.quote: The Senator supports robust environmental standards for any proposed data centers as well as greater transparency and local control over decisions to build
evidence.what_it_shows: Her campaign backs the 2025 state law making data centers pay full energy costs but did not answer the paper's direct questions about local moratoria or NDAs.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: She has pushed specific AI rules for years (deepfakes, election ads, whistleblowers, chatbots and toys, AI scams, gene synthesis screening) and is now the lead Democrat on a Senate bill for government oversight of the most dangerous frontier models. Safety advocates and Sen. Cantwell say her draft leans on company self-testing, so she sits between targeted guardrails and strict rules.

evidence.title: Nextgov: Klobuchar statement on the Cruz-Thune-Klobuchar frontier AI bill
evidence.quote: That includes requiring developers to work with government experts to verify and test models to make sure AI is safe. We cannot allow the release of dangerous models, including those that evade the control of their developers.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants binding government oversight of the riskiest models, but a Democratic committee aide called the draft 'primarily a voluntary standard type situation' and Cantwell is demanding mandatory national lab testing.

evidence.title: Press release: Klobuchar questions Sam Altman and Brad Smith at Senate Commerce AI hearing
evidence.quote: We want it to lead us to heaven, and I think we do that by making sure we have some rules of the road in place
evidence.what_it_shows: She framed her Thune bill as risk-based 'basic guardrails for the riskiest non-defense applications of AI' and got Altman to agree a risk-based approach is right.

evidence.title: Letter: Cantwell, Klobuchar, Markey ask CPSC to address AI chatbots in children's toys
evidence.quote: It is imperative that the manufacturers of these technologies be required to mitigate these risks before marketing toys to young children.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants mandatory risk mitigation before AI toys reach kids, a targeted binding rule.

evidence.title: Transcript: Senate Judiciary hearing 'Examining the Harm of AI Chatbots'
evidence.quote: One of the things that we know about these AI chatbots is that they are frequently designed to tell users what they want to hear
evidence.what_it_shows: She pressed grieving parents and experts on addictive companion bot design and whether parents should have a right to see their children's chatbot conversations.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1792 AI Whistleblower Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs protecting AI company workers who report safety problems to the government.

evidence.title: ARI release: Cotton and Klobuchar introduce Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her bipartisan bill would make mandatory the screening of synthetic DNA orders, aimed at AI lowering the barrier to designing dangerous pathogens.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.1213 Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban AI deepfakes of candidates meant to deceive voters, one of several election AI bills she leads.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4591 NO FAKES Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a federal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice and face; Roll Call named her a particular proponent when Judiciary advanced it in June 2026.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: A long-time Big Tech antitrust hawk who sponsors the main Senate antitrust reform bill, backs sunsetting Section 230, and cosponsors KOSA, COPPA 2.0 and the STOP CSAM Act. She says courts and current law are not enough and Congress must write new rules for dominant platforms.

evidence.title: Press release: Klobuchar statement on the Google antitrust remedy decision
evidence.quote: Today's ruling is a reminder of Google's sweeping power over the online economy, but the limited remedies ordered by the court demonstrate why we need additional rules of the road for Big Tech.
evidence.what_it_shows: She used the Google ruling to push her American Innovation and Choice Online Act against self-preferencing by dominant platforms.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.130 Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Her flagship bill would make big mergers harder and shift the burden to the largest companies.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3546 Sunset Section 230 Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would end platforms' liability shield in two years to force Congress to write new rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms toward minors.

evidence.title: Opening remarks at Judiciary subcommittee hearing on Meta whistleblowers and child safety
evidence.quote: Well, sorry is not enough anymore, and we need to put in some rules of the road to stop this from happening.
evidence.what_it_shows: As subcommittee ranking member she accused Meta of hiding child safety research and called for bipartisan rules.

evidence.title: Letter to DOJ and FTC urging antitrust probe of generative AI features on dominant platforms
evidence.quote: we urge the Department of Justice Antitrust Division and the Federal Trade Commission to investigate whether the design of some generative AI features, introduced by already dominant platforms, are a form of exclusionary conduct
evidence.what_it_shows: She led seven Democrats asking enforcers to treat AI summaries that keep users on Google and Meta as possible antitrust violations harming journalists.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.146 TAKE IT DOWN Act (now law)
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-authored with Sen. Cruz the law forcing platforms to remove nonconsensual intimate images and deepfakes within 48 hours.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

evidence.title: Cruz and Klobuchar statements marking one year of the TAKE IT DOWN Act as FTC enforcement begins
evidence.what_it_shows: The law's authors said platforms must now remove nonconsensual intimate images and deepfakes within 48 hours, with Cruz saying 'Big Tech can no longer look the other way' and Klobuchar noting platforms can no longer 'turn a blind eye.'

preemption.label: Leans states
preemption.summary: She cosponsored the States' Right to Regulate AI Act and wrote a New York Times op-ed arguing state AI laws keep people safe against Trump's preemption push. At the same time she is negotiating a national AI framework with Sens. Cruz and Thune that Sen. Cantwell warns would set a weak federal standard undermining state laws, so her final line on preemption depends on that bill.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3557 States' Right to Regulate AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Original cosponsor of Sen. Markey's bill saying the federal government cannot wipe out state AI rules; joined a week after the Dec. 11 executive order.

evidence.title: New York Times op-ed: 'State A.I. Laws Keep Us Safe. Trump's Next Move Could Upend That.'
evidence.what_it_shows: Headline seen via Google News; the page itself was blocked, so no verbatim text. The op-ed argued against Trump's planned executive order overriding state AI laws.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined the 99-1 vote to remove the moratorium; nearly every senator voted the same way, so the vote alone says little. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Nextgov: Klobuchar co-leading Cruz-Thune-Klobuchar national AI bill; Cantwell objects
evidence.quote: I'm continuing to work toward a bipartisan agreement on legislation for government oversight of the greatest risks posed by AI models
evidence.what_it_shows: Contradictory signal: she is drafting the national framework Republicans want; Cantwell posted that she opposes a 'weak federal standard' that undermines existing state AI legislation, so preemption terms remain the fight.

evidence.title: Cantwell and Senate Commerce Committee Democrats letter to Chairman Cruz demanding a markup of the reconciliation Commerce title, flagging the AI moratorium
evidence.what_it_shows: Twelve Commerce Committee Democrats told Cruz the AI moratorium 'tramples states' rights and holds the $42 billion BEAD program hostage' and asked for regular committee consideration instead of a fast-tracked floor vote.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Barrasso wants data centers and the power plants behind them built fast: he praised Trump's AI Action Plan for tearing down barriers to new data centers and is pushing a bill to break federal permitting bottlenecks. His one caveat is that data centers on federal land should get state and local input.

evidence.title: Senate floor speech: Barrasso: Whoever Powers the AI Revolution Will Win the AI Arms Race
evidence.quote: It tears down barriers to building new data centers. It encourages more private investment. Most importantly, it recognizes that America's AI future depends on America's energy future.
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrates the White House plan for removing obstacles to data center construction and ties it to Wyoming coal, gas and uranium.

evidence.title: Senate floor speech: Barrasso Calls on Senate to Fix America's Costly, Complex, and Cumbersome Permitting Process
evidence.quote: I will soon introduce legislation to break the bottlenecks in federal permitting. That is the number one way to boost American energy and mineral dominance.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants NEPA deadlines and limits on lawsuits so energy projects for the AI demand surge get built faster.

evidence.title: Cowboy State Daily: Developers Now Targeting Public Lands To Build Huge AI Data Centers (Barrasso comment)
evidence.quote: Development of federal land, including the construction of new data centers, deserves meaningful input from state and local governments and the public
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports the AI buildout but attaches a condition of local input when data centers go on federal land.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Barrasso treats AI as an arms race with China and applauds cutting regulations on AI developers. His stated AI worries are political bias in chatbots and Chinese theft of research, not safety rules on advanced models, though he did cosponsor the TAKE IT DOWN Act against AI sexual deepfakes.

evidence.title: Senate floor speech: Barrasso: Whoever Powers the AI Revolution Will Win the AI Arms Race
evidence.quote: President Trump recently announced an AI Action Plan. It releases American innovators from painful, punishing regulations.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI regulation as a burden to be lifted and puts winning the race with China first.

evidence.title: Senate Energy Committee hearing remarks: Barrasso: With Growth of AI and Other Critical Technologies, Labs Must Take China Threat Seriously
evidence.quote: We can't let political bias infiltrate development of AI. This is particularly true when taxpayer dollars are helping fund the technology's development.
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI concern is left-wing bias in chatbots like ChatGPT and security of taxpayer-funded research, not existential risk.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.146 TAKE IT DOWN Act (now law)

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Coons wants the US to build out AI computing but says that should not mean higher power bills or lost ground on climate. His answer is efficiency technology, co-leading a bill to study liquid cooling for data centers, not limits on new projects. No statement found on the proposed Delaware City data center itself.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Coons and McCormick introduce the Liquid Cooling for AI Act
evidence.quote: Leading the world in AI innovation shouldn't have to mean skyrocketing energy bills for American families or giving up ground in the fight against climate change
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports the AI buildout and the AI race but wants federal research to cut data center energy use and costs for families.

evidence.title: S.3269 Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 (original co-lead with Sen. McCormick)
evidence.what_it_shows: Directs a federal assessment of liquid cooling so AI data centers use less power; an efficiency approach rather than a pause or ratepayer mandate.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Coons backs a long list of specific AI rules: a federal right against AI voice and face copies, whistleblower protections, age checks for AI companion bots, bans on deceptive election deepfakes, and human control over military AI. At the same time he calls AI a race with China that America must win and attacked the Pentagon for punishing Anthropic and the White House for pulling frontier models offline without clear rules. He wants durable rules, not a pause.

evidence.title: S.4591 NO FAKES Act of 2026 (sponsor; also sponsored S.1367 in 2025 and S.4875 in 2024)
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature AI bill creates a legal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice or likeness; advanced out of Senate Judiciary in June 2026.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Senate Judiciary advances Coons's NO FAKES Act by voice vote
evidence.quote: Every American should have the right to decide how their voice and likeness will be used, especially when generative AI can create highly realistic digital replicas
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words at markup, he frames deepfake protection as a personal right that needs a binding federal law.

evidence.title: S.1792 AI Whistleblower Protection Act (cosponsor with Grassley)
evidence.what_it_shows: Protects AI company employees who report safety problems to the government, a targeted safety rule.

evidence.title: S.3062 GUARD Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require AI chatbot companies to verify ages and keep minors off AI companion bots.

evidence.title: Schatz-led letter from 10 senators to Meta CEO Zuckerberg on AI chatbots and children (Coons signed)
evidence.quote: The wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a bipartisan demand that Meta explain chatbot policies that allowed romantic talk with minors and add safeguards.

evidence.title: S.4707 Responsible Artificial Intelligence Defense Act of 2026 (sponsor with Reed)
evidence.what_it_shows: Sets rules for military AI that keep humans responsible for the use of force; the Senate Armed Services Committee folded its core into the FY2027 defense bill.

evidence.title: Press release: Ranking Member Coons statement on Pentagon-Anthropic dispute
evidence.quote: The Trump administration's decision to label Anthropic a supply chain risk to national security weakens free enterprise, harms innovation, and makes Americans less safe.
evidence.what_it_shows: He defended Anthropic's refusal to let its models be used for mass surveillance or fully autonomous weapons without a human off switch, calling those commonsense limits.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons statement on Anthropic's launch of Project Glasswing
evidence.quote: Now, Congress needs to step up and do our job: creating clear rules that encourage and support innovation and growth, while ensuring AI can't be used to threaten Americans.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants Congress to write clear AI rules, pairing innovation with guardrails and keeping the technology away from China.

evidence.title: Fortune: Gillibrand, Coons, Kelly, Schiff and Warner letter on the administration's 'unfocused, ad hoc' approach to frontier AI
evidence.quote: Without consistent policy governing American models, consumers and businesses would be incentivized to migrate to models from foreign vendors, including those based in the People's Republic of China.
evidence.what_it_shows: He criticized secret, sudden federal restrictions on frontier models and asked for a public, durable framework; his concern is predictability and competitiveness as much as safety.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons and Cotton introduce resolution affirming America's AI dominance
evidence.quote: The United States' prosperity and safety rests on our ability to win the AI race
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows his innovation-and-China framing; he wants frontier AI built in America by American companies, which tempers his guardrail stance.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Coons favors specific fixes for big platforms rather than break-ups: he cosponsors the Kids Online Safety Act and child-abuse-material bills, sponsors a bill forcing social media companies to open their data to researchers, and joined the letter pressing Meta on chatbots and kids. No support found for repealing Section 230 or breaking up companies.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor; also cosponsored S.1409 in the 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a duty of care and safety tools for minors on social media and games.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons and colleagues introduce the bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.quote: without proper safeguards, our children are too often exposed to objectionable, harmful, or outright dangerous content
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words, platforms have value but need mandated safeguards and more transparency about their effect on children.

evidence.title: S.3292 Platform Accountability and Transparency Act (sponsor with Cassidy; also S.1876 in the 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would force large social media companies to share data with independent researchers, a transparency rule rather than a structural remedy.

evidence.title: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would let victims sue platforms that fail to remove child sexual abuse material, a targeted carve-out from platform immunity.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Coons cosponsored the Senate GUARDRAILS Act, which would block the December 2025 executive order that pressures states to drop their AI laws. He voted with 98 other senators to strip the 10-year state AI law moratorium from the 2025 budget bill. No speech or statement in his own words on preemption was found, so this rests on his cosponsorship.

evidence.title: S.4216 GUARDRAILS Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Protects states' right to pass their own AI safety laws by stopping the executive order that would withhold federal funds from states that regulate AI.

evidence.title: Schatz press release: senators introduce legislation to repeal Trump's AI moratorium (lists Coons as cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Confirms Coons joined the six-senator bill introduced one week after the White House renewed its call to preempt state AI laws.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted to remove the moratorium, but the vote was 99 to 1 after a deal collapsed, so it is a weak signal on its own. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Coons is one of the Senate's most active Democrats on keeping advanced AI chips out of China. He condemned the H20 and H200 sales, co-led the SAFE Chips Act to lock current limits into law, cosponsored the Chip Security, GAIN AI and AI OVERWATCH Acts, and pressed Commerce Secretary Lutnick in writing when his testimony conflicted with Nvidia's CEO.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons statement on Trump's decision to allow export of advanced AI chips (H20) to China
evidence.quote: President Trump's decision today hands China cutting-edge technology that Beijing will use to erase our competitive advantage in artificial intelligence, undermine our military, and outpace our economy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed resuming H20 sales and demanded the decision be reversed.

evidence.title: Press release: Top Senate Democrats (Coons, Warner, Schumer, Reed, Warren) letter to Lutnick on resumed AI chip sales to China
evidence.quote: restricting access to leading-edge chips has been the defining barrier for the PRC's efforts to achieve AI parity
evidence.what_it_shows: Argues export controls are the key barrier to Chinese AI parity and objects to trading them away in trade talks.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Coons, Shaheen, Reed, Warner, Kelly, Himes, Krishnamoorthi on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: AI chips must only be exported to trusted companies, in reasonable numbers, and in concert with credible security standards and assurances.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposed large Gulf chip deals without safeguards against diversion to China.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons and Ricketts introduce SAFE Chips Act
evidence.quote: As China races to close our lead in AI, we cannot give them the technological keys to our future through advanced semiconductor chips.
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-led a bipartisan bill to write current chip export limits into law so the White House cannot loosen them alone.

evidence.title: S.3374 SAFE Chips Act of 2025 (co-lead)
evidence.what_it_shows: Codifies limits on the most advanced AI chips to China for 30 months.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons letter investigating Lutnick's statements on Nvidia H200 chip exports
evidence.quote: I believe that allowing any companies in China to purchase these products presents a serious risk to our national security and economic leadership
evidence.what_it_shows: Demanded the number of H200 chips licensed and shipped to China after Lutnick's testimony conflicted with Nvidia's CEO.

evidence.title: S.1705 Chip Security Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires location verification on exported advanced chips to stop smuggling into China.

evidence.title: S.3150 GAIN AI Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Makes chipmakers serve American buyers before shipping advanced AI chips to China.

evidence.title: S.4456 AI OVERWATCH Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Gives Congress a say before the government approves powerful AI chip sales to China and other risky countries.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Guthrie is the House's main mover on data center power costs: his committee passed the Ratepayer Protection Act 52-0 to make data centers pay for the grid upgrades they cause, and he is pushing for a floor vote. He is firmly pro-buildout, calls moratoriums harmful, says communities may opt out, and asked the FBI to probe whether China funds anti-data-center campaigns.

evidence.title: Opening statement: Guthrie leads efforts to lower energy costs, protect ratepayers (AI and the Grid legislative hearing)
evidence.quote: We are also ensuring that data centers are paying their fair share. Data centers should pay for the load that comes into the data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opened a hearing on seven data center and grid bills with the principle that data centers cover their own load costs.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Ratepayer Protection Act advances from committee 52-0
evidence.quote: The Ratepayer Protection Act will ensure that data centers pay their own way, instead of passing costs onto hardworking families.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shepherded H.R. 9340 through his committee unanimously despite data center industry objections.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Guthrie, Latta and Evans on introduction of the Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.quote: Winning the race to AI dominance is essential to securing America’s future global leadership, and that means expeditiously building the power infrastructure needed to support new technologies, while doing so in a responsible way
evidence.what_it_shows: Pairs a build-fast goal with the condition that families not foot the bill.

evidence.title: E&C ICYMI: Guthrie on Fox Business on AI policy, data center moratoriums and the Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.quote: We're about six months ahead of China and AI, people predict. If we had a year moratorium, let's say that's nationwide, and we get behind China, we'll never catch up.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposes data center moratoriums, criticized New York's, and says his bill helps states adopt the ratepayer pledge rather than imposing a one-size-fits-all federal rule.

evidence.title: E&C letter: Chairmen Guthrie, Joyce and Latta request investigation of foreign adversaries' efforts to block American data center buildout
evidence.quote: Americans deserve to know who is bankrolling the disinformation campaign that seeks to block critical infrastructure investments
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked PCAST and the FBI to investigate whether China-backed entities fund anti-data-center campaigns, treating organized opposition as possible foreign disinformation.

evidence.title: Bowling Green Daily News: Guthrie calls for investigations into AI and data center opposition, says local leaders decide
evidence.quote: The local concerns are real, and should be always taken into consideration
evidence.what_it_shows: Says communities may choose not to participate and that questions about taxes and jobs are fair, while insisting America must build or China will.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Guthrie pushes September floor vote on Ratepayer Protection Act despite industry pushback
evidence.quote: protects local communities and, I think, allows data centers to be successful
evidence.what_it_shows: Acknowledged data center industry opposition downtown but kept pressing leadership to bring the bill to the floor.

evidence.title: Politico: Guthrie says his data center bill aligns with Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge
evidence.quote: Our model is the Ratepayer Protection Pledge
evidence.what_it_shows: Positions the bill as bridging Trump's pro-data-center stance and vulnerable Republicans' constituent backlash.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Guthrie applauds White House announcement of $500 billion AI infrastructure investment
evidence.quote: This massive investment in American infrastructure makes clear that the United States is prepared to lead the world in next-generation technologies.
evidence.what_it_shows: Celebrated the Stargate data center build-out while flagging energy demand and permitting as challenges his committee would address.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Guthrie's AI doctrine is dominance, deployment and safeguards: beat China, avoid Europe-style rules, and add protections only where existing law falls short. The exception is kids and AI chatbots, where he backed the FTC inquiry, held a hearing and wrote chatbot safeguards into his KIDS Act.

evidence.title: Hatch Center essay by Guthrie: Dominance, Deployment, and Safeguards: The Path for American AI Leadership
evidence.quote: We are not in a race with Europe to regulate. We are in a race with China to innovate.
evidence.what_it_shows: Rejects EU-style AI regulation as growth-killing and puts innovation and China competition first.

evidence.title: Opening statement: full committee hearing on AI and American Global Competitiveness
evidence.quote: What I hear from people in this space, is that we have the brain power and we have the capital, what we need is the energy and the correct regulatory framework.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames AI as a war with China the US must win and says the committee's job is energy plus a light regulatory framework.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Guthrie on President Trump's AI Action Plan
evidence.quote: aligns with our Committee’s work to unleash infrastructure development and advanced manufacturing, promote a national AI framework, and safeguard Americans where existing protections fall short
evidence.what_it_shows: Endorsed the deregulatory action plan; new guardrails only where existing protections fall short.

evidence.title: E&C joint statement: Guthrie and Pallone applaud FTC inquiry into AI companion chatbots
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence has unleashed exponential levels of innovation, yet we are alarmed by recent incidents concerning the use of AI chatbots by minors.
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports targeted action on companion chatbots and children, the one area where he backs new rules.

evidence.title: E&C announcement: Oversight and Investigations hearing on the safety of AI chatbots
evidence.quote: additional oversight is needed to better understand risks to users when interacting with these technologies
evidence.what_it_shows: Convened a hearing on chatbot risks to children and teens while stressing AI's promise.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Guthrie wrote and passed the House's KIDS Act, which sets design, privacy and AI chatbot rules for platforms serving minors but drops the Senate's duty of care, and he is pushing a national privacy law that would override state laws without letting people sue. Targeted rules, not a Big Tech crackdown.

evidence.title: H.R.7757 KIDS Act (Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act), 119th
evidence.what_it_shows: His omnibus kids' online safety bill passed the House 267-117 on June 29, 2026 with chatbot disclosure, age verification and privacy rules but no duty of care.

evidence.title: Guthrie floor remarks on the KIDS Act
evidence.quote: The bill requires platforms to protect kids by default, including limiting addictive and dangerous design features and risky messaging functions.
evidence.what_it_shows: Describes binding design and default rules on platforms plus AI chatbot safeguards, framed as holding Big Tech accountable.

evidence.title: TechPolicy.Press: House GOP moves ahead with kids online safety package as Democrats balk (Guthrie markup remarks)
evidence.quote: the absence of a bipartisan consensus cannot be an excuse for inaction
evidence.what_it_shows: Pushed the package through committee 28-24 on party lines when talks broke down, then cut a bipartisan deal with Pallone in June.

evidence.title: Politico: House Republicans roll out landmark data privacy push (SECURE Data Act), Guthrie joint statement
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a national privacy standard from his working group that would preempt dozens of state privacy laws and bars private lawsuits; Pallone called it a bill written at the behest of Big Tech.

evidence.title: Opening statement: full committee hearing on AI and American Global Competitiveness (privacy remarks)
evidence.quote: We can’t do it in a heavy-handed way that stifles innovation
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants privacy and kids' protections but warns against heavy-handed regulation, pointing to Europe as the cautionary example.

evidence.title: Guthrie and Pallone joint statement supporting FTC inquiry into AI companion chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: The House Energy and Commerce chairman and ranking member jointly said they were 'alarmed' by incidents involving minors and chatbots, backed the FTC probe, and pledged bipartisan legislation to protect children online.

evidence.title: Speaker Johnson, Leader Scalise and Chairman Guthrie statements on House passage of the KIDS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: House Republican leaders hailed the 267-117 passage of the KIDS Act as protecting children while 'protecting free speech,' and Guthrie and Pallone jointly said it 'creates strong protections with new rules for design features, default settings, and kids' privacy.'

preemption.label: One national rule
preemption.summary: Guthrie is a leading House voice for one national AI rulebook. He signed the March 2026 leadership pledge to enact the White House framework preempting state AI laws, calls a patchwork of state laws a gift to adversaries, and said state preemption should come in the end even after his KIDS Act dropped it. His privacy bill would also override state privacy laws.

evidence.title: Joint statement: Johnson, Scalise, Guthrie, Jordan, Babin: House will work to implement National AI Framework
evidence.quote: House Republicans look forward to working across the aisle to enact a national framework that unleashes the full potential of AI, cements the U.S. as the global leader, and provides important protections for American families.
evidence.what_it_shows: Committed as E&C chairman to legislate the White House framework, which calls for broad preemption of state AI laws.

evidence.title: Hatch Center essay by Guthrie: Dominance, Deployment, and Safeguards
evidence.quote: A patchwork of state laws here at home would have the same effect, stalling AI development and deployment and providing our adversaries with opportunity to advance
evidence.what_it_shows: Equates state AI laws with Europe's growth-killing rules and argues for one national standard.

evidence.title: Record of Record: Guthrie signals state preemption remains the end goal after House kids' package
evidence.quote: We’re still gonna work it, and hopefully we’re gonna have to have state preemption in the end.
evidence.what_it_shows: Even after his bipartisan KIDS Act omitted AI preemption to win Democratic votes, he said preemption should be the final outcome.

evidence.title: Politico: House kids' safety deal complicates AI talks (KIDS Act omits AI preemption)
evidence.what_it_shows: His June 2026 deal with Pallone left out AI preemption and let states go further on kids' safety, a pragmatic exception to his preemption push.

evidence.title: E&C ICYMI: Guthrie on Fox Business on helping states adopt the Ratepayer Protection Pledge
evidence.quote: So we're not sending a federal statute out, we're assisting states to do so.
evidence.what_it_shows: On data center power costs he chose to help states rather than preempt them, so his preemption drive is about AI and privacy rules, not energy siting.

evidence.title: Breitbart: Leading the Future super PAC endorses second slate of House Republicans including Guthrie
evidence.what_it_shows: The AI industry super PAC that campaigns for federal preemption of state AI laws endorsed him for reelection.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Hoeven has not spoken directly about data centers in anything we found. His related record is pro-build: he sponsors a bill to move coal, gas and nuclear plants to the front of the grid connection line to meet rising demand, and he wants states and existing ratepayers shielded from transmission cost shifts.

evidence.title: Press release: Hoeven, Young introduce GRID Power Act (S. 465) to fast-track baseload power projects
evidence.quote: Our legislation seeks to reverse this trend by empowering grid operators to put baseload power generation projects at the front of the line for approval.
evidence.what_it_shows: His answer to rising electricity demand, which the bill's backers tie to AI data centers, is to build more always-on generation faster.

evidence.title: Press release: Cramer, Fedorchak introduce FAIR Act; Hoeven cosponsors the Senate companion (S. 3287)
evidence.quote: North Dakotans shouldn’t be forced to pay higher energy costs to help other states meet their unworkable energy mandates
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants electric bills protected from cost shifting, a ratepayer-first instinct he applies to transmission built for other states rather than to data centers specifically.

evidence.title: E&E News: North Dakota delegation letter to FERC on transmission cost allocation; delegation guards state planning authority
evidence.what_it_shows: E&E reports Hoeven joined a September 2025 letter urging FERC not to assign regional transmission costs to North Dakotans who do not benefit, and describes the delegation as steadfast in preserving state planning autonomy as Washington pushes faster data center grid hookups.

evidence.title: Press release: Hoeven presses FERC nominees on baseload power and states' rights
evidence.quote: We need policies that support a diverse mix of energy resources to ensure grid stability and resilience, while also respecting the rights of states and private landowners.
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties meeting rising electricity demand to coal-fired baseload power and to respecting state regulators and landowners.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (119th S. 1748)

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (118th S. 1409)
evidence.what_it_shows: He also cosponsored the earlier version that passed the Senate in July 2024.

evidence.title: Press release: Hoeven on Senate passage of KOSA and COPPA 2.0
evidence.quote: This legislation takes responsible, measured steps to hold online platforms accountable for the content that minors can access on their sites, while better empowering parents to ensure their children remain safe online.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he supports holding platforms accountable for harms to minors, framed as measured rather than sweeping.

evidence.title: KFYR-TV: Where does TikTok stand in the US Senate?
evidence.quote: People will still have their TikTok, it’s just that it should not be owned and controlled by the Chinese Communist Party.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pushed the Senate to pass the forced-sale TikTok bill on national security grounds.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Senate roll call 363, Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1)

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Johnson calls AI an enormously complex problem and is skeptical that Congress can write good rules for it, saying the country would be better off passing far fewer laws. He is also wary of trusting industry experts with vested interests, so he has not embraced any specific AI guardrail bill.

evidence.title: Fox News: State-level AI rules survive as Senate sinks moratorium despite White House pressure
evidence.quote: And I think we'd be far better off if we passed a lot fewer laws. I'm not sure how often we get it right.
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked about a federal AI framework, he doubted Congress should legislate much on AI at all.

evidence.title: Fox News: State-level AI rules survive as Senate sinks moratorium despite White House pressure
evidence.quote: And again, I'm concerned, the real experts on this have got vested interests. Whatever they're advising is, can you really trust them?
evidence.what_it_shows: He is skeptical of the AI industry's advice as well, so his light-touch stance is not a pro-industry one.

tech_regulation.label: Mixed
tech_regulation.summary: Johnson has long attacked what he calls Big Tech censorship, cosponsoring bills to expose government pressure on platforms and joining a 2022 call to ban TikTok from state devices. evidence.title: Press release: Sen. Johnson joins Sen. Hagerty, colleagues in reintroducing the Disclose Government Censorship Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He cosponsored a bill requiring transparency when the government asks platforms to suppress speech, his main approach to Big Tech.

evidence.quote: I personally don't think we should be setting a federal standard right now and prohibiting the states from doing what we should be doing in a federated republic. Let the states experiment
evidence.what_it_shows: He came out against the moratorium before the Senate vote on federalism grounds.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (99-1)

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Paul says whether to allow a data center should be a local or state decision, not Washington's. He opposes a federal ban and federal subsidies alike, calls the boom overhyped, and wants more nuclear power to feed it.

evidence.title: Bowling Green Daily News interview: Paul on data centers
evidence.quote: I think people won’t be very satisfied with someone who’s so distant from the problem making the decision
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants siting decided locally; the paper reports he opposes both a federal ban on data centers and federal funding for them, and will not dictate local zoning.

evidence.title: Oldham Era interview: Senator weighs in on data centers
evidence.quote: Nobody in Washington can know as well or feel as strongly about these types of issues as the people who are close to them so I would keep these decisions local
evidence.what_it_shows: Repeats that data center decisions belong to local jurisdictions, while voicing concern about federal moves to expand data centers.

evidence.title: WLKY: Paul at Fort Knox on data centers after Gov. Beshear's executive order
evidence.quote: We shouldn't tell them they have to, nor should we tell them they can't. I think the decision should be made the more local, the better
evidence.what_it_shows: Neither a federal push nor a federal block; he also called the data center rush hype that will cool and said fewer may be needed than claimed.

evidence.title: Kentucky Lantern: Paul says states will decide AI and data center policy, wants more nuclear power
evidence.quote: You can’t just have data centers without energy, so we’re going to need more energy
evidence.what_it_shows: Ties data center growth to new power supply, backs nuclear and coal, and expects state legislatures to make most of these calls.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Paul treats AI as inevitable and mostly beneficial in private hands and opposes new federal mandates on platforms. His AI worry is government using AI to surveil and censor citizens, where he wants hard limits. Mixed, but leans light touch on industry.

evidence.title: Oldham Era interview: Paul on AI's future and government surveillance
evidence.quote: I think AI will bring benefits, particularly in the private industry and private world, but where I see potential problems with AI are in government's use in spying or surveilling on its citizenry.
evidence.what_it_shows: Locates the danger in government use of AI, not in the technology or the companies building it.

evidence.title: National Review op-ed: Keep Artificial Intelligence out of Government Surveillance
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is only going to make it easier for the government to do this and harder to detect.
evidence.what_it_shows: Calls for getting to the bottom of federal AI-driven disinformation monitoring, a civil-liberties guardrail on government rather than industry regulation.

evidence.title: HSGAC hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Government: Paul warns of AI surveillance threat to free expression
evidence.what_it_shows: As ranking member he used the committee's AI hearing to attack federal use of AI tools to flag and suppress speech, and sought limits on that use.

tech_regulation.label: Mixed
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed. Paul was one of three senators to vote against the Kids Online Safety Act and sponsored a bill to repeal the TikTok ban, calling both censorship. But in January 2026 he reversed on Section 230 and vowed legislation to strip Google and YouTube's liability shield, and he backs limits on the government buying Americans' data.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 221 (2024): passage of S.2073 Kids Online Safety and Privacy Act (Nay)
evidence.what_it_shows: One of only three senators against the kids' online safety package that passed 91-3. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: Courier Journal op-ed against KOSA, as quoted by The Hill
evidence.quote: This requirement will not only stifle free speech, but it will deprive Americans of the benefits of our technological advancements.
evidence.what_it_shows: He objected to KOSA's duty of care as a speech restriction; the quote is from The Hill's report on his op-ed.

evidence.title: New York Post: Paul says KOSA will lead to censorship
evidence.quote: But I’m afraid it will lead to censorship.
evidence.what_it_shows: Sympathetic to the goal but argues a vague anxiety standard enforced by the FTC would let government censor content.

evidence.title: S.153 Repeal the TikTok Ban Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would undo the law forcing TikTok's sale or ban, the opposite of his Kentucky colleague McConnell.

evidence.title: Press release: Paul and Khanna introduce Repeal the TikTok Ban Act
evidence.quote: A government that can ban an app, can ban a book. A government that can silence a platform, can silence a person.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames the TikTok ban as government control of speech rather than a China security measure.

evidence.title: New York Post op-ed reversing on Section 230, as quoted by Broadband Breakfast
evidence.quote: The arrogance of Google to continue hosting this defamatory video and the resultant threats on my life have caused me to rethink Congress’ blind allegiance to liability shields
evidence.what_it_shows: After YouTube refused to remove a video he calls defamatory, he pledged to pursue legislation ending Section 230 protections, a sharp turn toward reining in Big Tech.

evidence.title: S.2425 Free Speech Protection Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Bars officials from pressuring platforms to take down posts; a restraint on government, not a platform rule.

evidence.title: S.2576 Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would stop police and spy agencies from buying Americans' location and phone data from brokers without a warrant.

evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the effort to pull the 10-year freeze on state AI laws out of the GOP reconciliation bill before it reached the floor.

evidence.quote: a lot of these decisions will be made by the state legislature
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked how federal AI decisions would affect state policy, he pointed to state legislatures as the deciders.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Cramer is an enthusiastic booster of AI data centers in North Dakota, calling it a race with China and telling companies to bring their own on-site power. He pairs that with conditions: states must keep their planning authority over grid hookups, and other ratepayers should not be stuck with the bill.

evidence.title: WDAY Radio: Senator Cramer urges urgency, local power to fuel North Dakota's AI revolution
evidence.quote: This is a race right now, it is the fourth industrial revolution.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants North Dakota to build AI data centers fast, calls it data farming, and urges companies to put power generation on site behind the meter rather than lean on regulated utilities.

evidence.title: The Flag (AM 1100): Cramer on Armada's modular AI data center arriving at GrandSKY
evidence.quote: We have to be careful not to go too slow
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrated a new data center project he helped recruit, framed the buildout as a technology race with China, and said modular designs can answer public concerns about energy use.

evidence.title: E&E News: Wright's data center push draws Republican scrutiny
evidence.quote: We have to strike a balance that doesn’t completely dismiss a state’s rights or, you know, reduce the importance of or diminish the importance of a planning process.
evidence.what_it_shows: As a former state utility regulator he is uncertain about a federal push to speed data center grid hookups if it sidelines state planning, and wants states a path to appeal FERC decisions.

evidence.title: Press release: Cramer, Fedorchak introduce FAIR Act (Cramer sponsors Senate companion S. 3287)
evidence.quote: Too often, ratepayers in North Dakota are left holding the bag after the dust settles on failed energy policies enacted by other states.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a user-pay rule so electric bills are not shifted onto people who do not benefit from new transmission lines.

evidence.title: Grand Forks Herald: AI firm unveils mobile data center at Grand Sky event (Cramer remarks)
evidence.quote: This just becomes one more tool to attract, not just another Northrop Grumman or General Atomics, but another inventor, another college student
evidence.what_it_shows: Speaking at the unveiling, he called the data center one more tool to attract defense firms and inventors to Grand Forks, showing he treats these projects as economic wins.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Cramer talks about AI as a race with China that America must win by building faster and getting government out of the way; we found no statements treating advanced AI as a danger needing new federal rules. He did oppose blocking states from regulating AI, so he is not purely hands-off.

evidence.title: WDAY Radio: Cramer on the AI revolution and North Dakota's role
evidence.quote: This is a race right now, it is the fourth industrial revolution.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI as an economic race to win, not a risk to contain, and says the state should get out of its own way.

evidence.title: Ricketts-led letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick calling for a stable regulatory environment to win the AI race (Cramer signed)
evidence.quote: The Trump administration should not return to Biden’s tiers and caps that confused close allies and partners.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined senators praising the administration for unshackling AI and asking for lighter, predictable rules so American AI can spread abroad.

evidence.title: Punchbowl News: GOP resistance to AI moratorium intensifies (Cramer against Cruz proposal)
evidence.what_it_shows: Counterpoint: he told Punchbowl he opposed forcing states to choose between regulating AI and getting federal AI infrastructure money, so he did not want state AI guardrails wiped out.

evidence.what_it_shows: He backs banning connected cars and car software from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea.

evidence.what_it_shows: He supported forcing TikTok's sale on national security grounds.

evidence.quote: Big tech, the corporate media, and the Administration have no credibility in determining what is and isn’t ‘misinformation,’

preemption.label: Leans states
preemption.summary: Before the Senate vote, Cramer told Punchbowl News he opposed Sen. Cruz's plan to make states choose between regulating AI and getting federal AI infrastructure money, then voted to strip the 10-year moratorium. evidence.title: Punchbowl News: GOP resistance to AI moratorium intensifies

No statement found on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales.

evidence.title: Press release: Cramer, Kim introduce legislation to ensure American export security

data_centers.label: Build faster

His committee also blocked a Democratic amendment on data centers' community impacts.

evidence.quote: Permitting delays for power generation and transmission, environmental review bottlenecks, and regulatory uncertainty slow the construction and expansion of critical infrastructure.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Comer celebrates the $100 billion Paducah AI hub in his district and says America must build data centers or China will. But he wants them to be a local decision, pay for everything themselves and receive no incentives.

evidence.title: WPSD Local 6: Kentucky officials weigh in on Paducah American Energy Hub
evidence.quote: We certainly are very happy about the the progress with the data center and the investment that's been made and the jobs that are being created.
evidence.what_it_shows: Welcomed the $100B hyperscale campus in his district and credited the president's support for nuclear power.

evidence.title: WPSD Local 6: Comer discusses AI data centers at Paducah Chamber event
evidence.quote: I think as long as the community wants a data center, as long as the data center pays for everything, and they don't get incentivized, then I think it can be a good thing for the community.
evidence.what_it_shows: Sets conditions: local consent, full cost coverage and no tax incentives; he called data centers controversial.

evidence.title: WPSD Local 6: Comer on data centers and China at Paducah Chamber event
evidence.quote: If we don't have them in the United States, they're going to be built in China, and we don't want data centers built in China
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames data centers as a national necessity in the race with China, which keeps him on the pro-build side despite his conditions.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Comer's AI concerns run through government: he sponsored a bill making agencies disclose the AI they use, and in 2026 demanded answers on D.C.'s plan to use AI cameras to flag property violations and on OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's finances. No position found on frontier AI safety rules, licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: H.R.7532 Federal A.I. Governance and Transparency Act of 2024 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make federal agencies track the AI they use and tell the public how they use it, a transparency rule aimed at government rather than industry.

evidence.title: Oversight press release: Comer letter to D.C. Department of Buildings on AI surveillance of property owners
evidence.quote: the Committee is concerned about the potential of this initiative to ensnare District property owners in a regime of excessive fees, external property maintenance violations, and unpayable tax debt
evidence.what_it_shows: Raised alarm about a government using AI camera surveillance to generate fines, an oversight-of-government use of AI rather than an industry rule.

evidence.title: PYMNTS: Oversight Chairman Comer letter to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on potential conflicts of interest
evidence.quote: The Committee aims to ensure that funds donated for charitable purposes are not diverted for unintended uses, such as artificially increasing the market value of other companies in which an executive or board member may hold an interest
evidence.what_it_shows: Scrutiny of the leading AI lab focused on nonprofit money and executive conflicts, not model safety.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Comer backs targeted checks on tech platforms: a probe of AI-driven surveillance pricing at Uber, Lyft, Expedia and others, and the App Store Freedom Act to open Apple and Google's app stores. His longest-running tech fight is against government pressure on platforms to censor, which restrains government rather than companies, so he is no Big Tech trust-buster.

evidence.title: American Bazaar (citing Reuters): Comer letters to five travel and delivery companies on AI surveillance pricing
evidence.quote: for companies to weaponize personal data and pad their profit margins at the expense of providing transparency to consumers
evidence.what_it_shows: Opened an investigation into AI-driven personalized pricing, a consumer-protection push against tech platforms.

evidence.title: H.R.3209 App Store Freedom Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would force Apple and Google to allow outside apps and app stores, a targeted rule on the two gatekeepers.

evidence.title: H.R.140 Protecting Speech from Government Interference Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Bans federal workers from pressuring social media companies to remove posts; a restraint on government, not a platform mandate.

evidence.title: Press release: Comer applauds House passage of bill to protect Americans from censorship
evidence.quote: The Biden Administration has eroded Americans’ First Amendment rights by bullying social media companies to censor certain views and news on their platforms.
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature Big Tech issue is government-driven censorship, which does not translate into support for breaking up or regulating the companies.

evidence.quote: These incidents mark the first publicly confirmed instances of a frontier AI model autonomously launching unauthorized attacks on real people and companies, underscoring the urgent need for federal oversight of frontier AI systems
evidence.what_it_shows: She demanded timelines, model instructions, security logs and transcripts, and called for federal testing standards, containment rules and disclosure requirements for powerful AI systems.

evidence.title: Fox News: Blunt Rochester letter to Anthropic on repeated model attacks during evaluations
evidence.quote: Anthropic models' repeated attacks on third parties with no knowledge of, or role in, Anthropic and AISI's evaluations demonstrate an alarming pattern of malicious behavior
evidence.what_it_shows: Treats autonomous model misbehavior as a serious safety problem requiring government answers, not just voluntary company review.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester and Sheehy introduce AI Fraud Accountability Act
evidence.quote: With more Americans using AI every day, we need to do all we can to cut down on AI-related fraud
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-led a bipartisan bill making realistic AI impersonation to defraud people a federal offense enforced by the FTC.

evidence.title: S.3982 AI Fraud Accountability Act of 2026 (co-lead with Sheehy)
evidence.what_it_shows: Adds criminal and civil penalties for using AI to trick or scam people.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester questions OpenAI CEO Sam Altman at Commerce hearing on winning the AI race
evidence.quote: making sure that we are watching out for ethics, watching out for scams, watching out that technology does not take over the human [race]
evidence.what_it_shows: She voiced excitement about AI's opportunities while naming ethics, scams and loss of human control as concerns, and pressed Altman on OpenAI's shift to a for-profit structure.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Blunt Rochester, Hirono and Schiff introduce the Workforce of the Future Act
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is increasingly disrupting our economy, contributing to layoffs and occupational changes
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants federal agencies to study AI's job impact and fund worker training, a targeted response to AI displacement.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Blunt Rochester presses Fed Chair Warsh on who sits on the Fed's AI task force
evidence.quote: I hope that there will be the inclusion of other voices beyond economic experts and tech individuals, but actually families, businesses, people that are actually both consuming and impacted by AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked the Fed to give Main Street equal footing with Wall Street and tech leaders when weighing AI and jobs.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester and Curtis launch Consumer Safety Technology Act
evidence.quote: Our government must be able to keep up with new and emerging technologies, especially when it comes to consumer safety
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows her pro-adoption side: she wants agencies like the Consumer Product Safety Commission to use AI to protect consumers.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: She goes after platforms on specific harms rather than structure: she led eight senators demanding that X, Meta, Alphabet, Snap, Reddit and TikTok explain and remove sexualized AI deepfakes, cosponsors the Kids Online Safety Act, and backs a bill to stop fentanyl sales on social media. No calls found for breaking up Big Tech or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester leads 8 senators in letter to tech companies demanding removal of sexualized AI-generated images
evidence.quote: users are finding ways around these guardrails. Or these guardrails are failing. Even where outputs do not depict explicit nudity, they can still be non-consensual, sexualizing, and harmful. The public deserves transparency.
evidence.what_it_shows: Demanded that six platforms hand over policies, preserve documents, and explain how they remove AI undressing deepfakes and notify victims.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care and safety tools for minors on social media, games and video sites.

evidence.title: S.3618 No Fentanyl on Social Media Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Pushes platforms to stop drug sales on their apps, a targeted platform rule.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Blunt Rochester has repeatedly defended states' power to regulate AI. As a Commerce Committee Democrat she signed the June 2025 letter calling the 10-year moratorium an attack on states' rights, said in July 2025 that partisanship should not shroud the ability of states and Congress to regulate AI, and cosponsored the GUARDRAILS Act to block the December 2025 executive order.

evidence.title: Cantwell and Commerce Committee Democrats letter to Chairman Cruz on the reconciliation Commerce title (Blunt Rochester signed)
evidence.quote: the AI moratorium proposal tramples states' rights and holds the $42 billion BEAD program hostage, further delaying the broadband Americans desperately need
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposed the state AI law moratorium before the Senate vote, on states' rights grounds.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester statement on Trump administration's executive actions on AI
evidence.quote: I do not believe that we should allow culture wars and deep partisanship to shroud the ability of states and Congress to regulate this rapidly evolving industry.
evidence.what_it_shows: In her own words, states should keep the ability to regulate AI alongside Congress.

evidence.title: S.4216 GUARDRAILS Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would stop the December 2025 executive order from withholding federal funds from states that pass AI safeguards; confirmed on the Schatz press release listing cosponsors.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted to remove the moratorium; consistent with her letters, though the 99 to 1 vote is weak evidence by itself. Recorded vote: Yea.

preemption.label: One national rule

evidence.what_it_shows: House GOP leadership endorsed the White House framework, which calls for blocking state AI laws that impose 'undue burdens' in favor of a single national standard.

evidence.what_it_shows: He called China an 'adversary' after Beijing told firms to stop buying Nvidia chips, hawkish rhetoric without a stated position on US export limits.
