pacs.agenda: Elect 'pro-innovation, pro-AI' candidates of both parties; push a single national AI framework / federal preemption over state AI laws; oppose candidates who back state AI-safety statutes (chief targe
pacs.detail: Endorsed on Apr 16, 2026 GOP Champions list.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Joyce pushes hard to build data centers, framing the buildout as a race with China and asking the FBI to investigate whether foreign adversaries are behind local opposition. At the same time he cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act to keep big users' grid costs off household electric bills. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: The only data-center evidence is a letter he co-signed calling the Sanders moratorium bill 'disastrous', casting local/state pauses as possibly foreign-directed, and asking the FBI to investigate opponents of buildout. T

evidence.title: Letter: Chairmen Guthrie, Joyce and Latta ask PCAST and FBI Director Patel to investigate foreign efforts to block U.S. data center buildout
evidence.quote: The U.S. is in a global race for technological superiority that has significantly raised the stakes for economic and national security if our nation falls behind.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats data-center construction as critical national infrastructure and calls the Sanders data-center moratorium bill disastrous, a strongly pro-buildout stance.

evidence.title: Data Center Dynamics: Trio of Republicans call for FBI investigation into data center opposition
evidence.quote: foreign influence campaigns… have engaged in a coordinated effort to slow US growth in AI development and the building of infrastructure supporting AI data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: Trade press coverage of the same letter shows Joyce casting grassroots data-center opposition as possibly foreign-directed rather than a legitimate local concern.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a bill to stop regular customers' electric bills from rising to pay for power that large new users like data centers need, a condition on the buildout.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on SPEED Act permitting reform (House roll call 356)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to speed federal permitting for energy and infrastructure projects, consistent with a build-faster approach to the power needed for AI. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. As Oversight chairman Joyce held hearings warning that AI chatbots can harm vulnerable users and that AI-designed biology is outrunning existing safeguards, and said current oversight must be re-examined. But he also frames AI as a race with China, promotes AI medical devices, and was endorsed by the industry-funded Leading the Future super PAC.

evidence.title: Opening statement: O&I hearing on the risks and benefits of AI chatbots
evidence.quote: It is important that we consider the implications of these technologies as we balance the benefits of AI innovation with protecting the most vulnerable among us.
evidence.what_it_shows: He convened a hearing on chatbot harms to children and people with mental illness and welcomed the FTC inquiry, a guardrail-minded but balanced posture.

evidence.title: Opening statement: O&I hearing on biosecurity at the intersection of AI and biology
evidence.quote: the federal government must continue to carefully assess whether our current safeguards and reporting systems are adequate in an era of rapidly advancing AI technology.
evidence.what_it_shows: He said AI tools that can help design dangerous pathogens introduce profound new risks and that existing oversight frameworks may not cover them.

evidence.title: Letter: Guthrie, Joyce and Latta request investigation of efforts to slow American AI progress
evidence.quote: The U.S. is in a global race for technological superiority that has significantly raised the stakes for economic and national security if our nation falls behind.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI primarily as a competition with China and treats efforts to slow AI development as a threat, a light-touch signal.

evidence.title: Press release: Dr. Joyce introduces Health Tech Investment Act to improve access to AI healthcare devices
evidence.quote: The bipartisan Health Tech Act will ensure that American patients, regardless of rural or urban care settings, can access new, innovative AI-enabled medical devices that are revolutionizing healthcare.
evidence.what_it_shows: He is an enthusiast for deploying AI in medicine and wants Medicare to pay for AI-enabled devices faster.

evidence.title: Breitbart: Leading the Future super PAC releases list of House GOP Champions
evidence.quote: part of a broader ecosystem of current members who have engaged with the industry
evidence.what_it_shows: The $100 million-plus AI industry super PAC named Joyce a champion, meaning the industry views him as an ally on a national framework with basic rather than strict rules.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Joyce wrote and sponsored the House Republicans' comprehensive consumer privacy bill, the SECURE Data Act, with FTC and state attorney general enforcement, and has cosponsored robocall, TikTok and kids' privacy bills. Critics on the left call his privacy bill too friendly to industry, and he has also pressed platforms over alleged censorship of conservatives.

evidence.title: Sponsor: SECURE Data Act (H.R. 8413), comprehensive federal consumer privacy bill
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the lead author of the first major federal privacy bill of the 119th Congress, giving consumers rights to access, correct, delete and opt out of sale of their data.

evidence.title: Press release: Guthrie and Joyce announce creation of E&C privacy working group
evidence.quote: We strongly believe that a national data privacy standard is necessary to protect Americans' rights online and maintain our country's global leadership in digital technologies, including artificial intelligence.
evidence.what_it_shows: He launched and leads the GOP working group that produced the privacy bill, tying data rules to AI leadership.

evidence.title: HIPAA Journal: House Republicans introduce federal data privacy legislation (Guthrie-Joyce joint statement)
evidence.quote: This bill establishes clear, enforceable protections so that Americans remain in charge of their own data and companies are held accountable for its safe keeping
evidence.what_it_shows: He describes the bill as enforceable accountability for companies, a targeted-rules stance; the article notes it was drafted without Democratic input.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Foreign Robocall Elimination Act (H.R. 6152)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports a specific fix cracking down on scam robocalls from abroad.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (H.R. 7521, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed forcing TikTok's sale or ban over Chinese control.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (H.R. 7890, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported stronger privacy protections for kids and teens online.

evidence.title: In the news: Dr. Joyce pushes for answers on censorship and conservative bias from Big Tech
evidence.quote: Shutting down the Adams County Republican Committee Facebook page strikes me as an infringement on speech that is normally protected in the public domain.
evidence.what_it_shows: He has confronted Facebook and Twitter CEOs over content moderation, a conservative angle on holding platforms accountable.

preemption.label: Leans national rule
preemption.summary: Joyce has not spoken directly about a moratorium on state AI laws, but his privacy bill would override state privacy laws, he argues industry wants one federal standard instead of a state-by-state patchwork, and he voted for the House budget bill that carried the 10-year AI moratorium. He leans toward one national standard.

evidence.title: Roll Call: GOP data privacy bill tries again to set national standard
evidence.quote: They said industry came to us and said, 'Please, not one more. This should be done at a federal level. We're playing whack-a-mole. Industries cross state lines.'
evidence.what_it_shows: He makes the classic preemption argument, that a patchwork of state laws should be replaced by one federal rule, in the privacy debate that runs parallel to the AI fight.

evidence.title: IAPP analysis: SECURE Data Act would preempt state privacy laws
evidence.quote: As introduced, the SECURE Data Act would embrace a strong preemption regime, rendering moot any state law or provision that 'relates to' its provisions.
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill takes a broad preemption approach, wiping out state consumer privacy laws and data broker registries.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 1 reconciliation bill containing the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws (House roll call 145)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the House version of the budget bill that included the state AI-law moratorium; a party-line vote on a huge bill, so weak evidence on its own. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: WTMJ: Steil: Don't stick families with AI costs
evidence.what_it_shows: Headline seen in Google News results; the page returned 403 and no archive copy exists. A first-pass summary says he attended Microsoft's Washington announcement of its community-first plan shifting costs onto the company and said it could set a national standard.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Hawley is the Missouri delegation's loudest critic of data center power costs. He says data centers are fine if they create jobs, but wants a binding law forcing them to pay for their own electricity and water, and he sponsors the GRID Act to keep them off the regular grid.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley and Blumenthal introduce the GRID Act (S.3852) to stop data centers from raising consumer electricity bills
evidence.quote: American families should not have to shoulder the burden of the rising electricity costs produced by data centers in Missouri and across the country. This is unacceptable
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would bar consumer rate increases tied to data centers, give households grid priority, and require new data centers to use off-grid power.

evidence.title: St. Louis Public Radio interview: Hawley says ratepayers should not subsidize data centers
evidence.quote: If data centers are going to come into the state, fine. If they're going to create jobs? Hey, wonderful. But if they're going to suck up a bunch of electricity, they need to pay for that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He does not oppose data centers outright but conditions them on paying their own way, putting him at odds with Gov. Kehoe and Rep. Jason Smith.

evidence.title: Letter to Ameren CEO demanding answers on rate hikes, shut-offs and data center deals
evidence.quote: I am concerned Ameren is seeking dramatic rate increases in order to supply massive data centers and industrial users.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed Missouri's largest utility on whether residential customers are cross-subsidizing data center contracts.

evidence.title: Warren-Hawley letter to the Energy Information Administration seeking mandatory data center energy reporting
evidence.quote: Comprehensive information regarding the operations of data centers and other large loads is essential for accurate grid planning and will support policymaking to prevent large companies from increasing electricity costs for American families
evidence.what_it_shows: A left-right push for mandatory disclosure so the public can check whether data centers pay their share.

evidence.title: Missourinet: Hawley wants Trump's ratepayer protection pledge written into law
evidence.quote: I think we ought to say in the law that the data centers have to pay for their own electricity, the data centers have to pay for their own water supply.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats the White House's voluntary pledge as insufficient and wants binding law covering both power and water.

evidence.title: Free Press op-ed: AI Will Control Us If We Do Not Control It (cites the Festus, Mo. data center fight)
evidence.quote: The companies building these facilities can afford to supply their own power, protect residential rates, and safeguard local water. We must hold them to that with binding legal requirements, not hollow promises.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames data centers as a cost shifted onto working families and demands legally binding conditions.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Hawley wants binding rules now. He sponsors mandatory federal safety testing of the most powerful AI models, product liability for AI harms, a ban on AI companions for minors, and AI layoff reporting, and in Sept. 2026 he opened a Senate probe of OpenAI citing existential risk.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley and Blumenthal introduce the Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act (S.2938)
evidence.quote: This bipartisan legislation would guarantee common-sense testing and oversight of the most advanced AI systems, so Congress and the American people can be better informed about potential risks
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would make advanced AI systems go through a mandatory Energy Department evaluation program before release.

evidence.title: Press release and letter: Chairman Hawley launches investigation into OpenAI for the Hugging Face hack and existential risk of AI products
evidence.quote: My investigation will probe this AI hacking incident, along with growing allegations of the existential risk of new AI products.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats frontier AI as a potential existential danger and is using subcommittee oversight powers on a leading lab.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Hawley reacts to Trump executive order setting voluntary cyber reviews of advanced AI
evidence.quote: I would go farther. I think we ought to enact my legislation that I have with Senator [Richard] Blumenthal that would make that sort of reporting and monitoring mandatory
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the order but said voluntary review is not enough and mandatory testing should be law.

evidence.title: Axios AI+DC Summit: Hawley pushes ban on AI chatbots for minors (GUARD Act, S.3062)
evidence.quote: The first thing we need to do is we need to pass legislation that would prevent AI chatbots from targeting minor children
evidence.what_it_shows: His GUARD Act, which the Judiciary Committee later passed 22-0, would ban AI companions for minors and add criminal penalties for chatbots that sexualize children.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI LEAD Act (S.2937), product liability for AI systems
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs letting people hurt by AI sue the developer like any other defective product.

evidence.title: Sponsor: AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act (S.3108)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require companies to report AI-driven layoffs to the government.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI Whistleblower Protection Act (S.1792)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports legal protection for AI company employees who report safety problems.

evidence.title: Blumenthal-Hawley Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act (licensing regime, liability, transparency)
evidence.quote: Congress must act on AI regulation, and these principles should form the backbone
evidence.what_it_shows: As far back as 2023 he proposed licensing sophisticated general-purpose models through an independent oversight body.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley warns 'AI threatens the working man' at NatCon 5
evidence.quote: millions of Americans out of work. That's not any conspiracy theory, by the way. That's what the tech titans openly tell us.
evidence.what_it_shows: He casts AI as a threat to jobs and liberty and says protecting children should be the lodestar for guardrails.

evidence.title: Washington Examiner: Public First Action launches $15 million project featuring Hawley among pro-guardrail Republicans
evidence.what_it_shows: An AI safety group is spending to promote him, along with Sens. Cotton and Moody and Rep. Donalds, as Republicans who back AI guardrails.

evidence.title: Hawley op-ed, 'AI Will Control Us If We Do Not Control It' (The Free Press)
evidence.what_it_shows: Hawley argued the federal government must set binding rules on AI jobs impacts, data centers and child safety, that AI 'is a question of self-government' that 'cannot be left to' Silicon Valley, and that the final stake is 'the conquest of some men by other men.'

evidence.title: Hawley, Blumenthal and Padilla remarks at Senate Judiciary markup of the GUARD Act (22-0 vote)
evidence.what_it_shows: At the unanimous committee vote to ban AI companions for minors, Hawley said a beneficial AI age 'is a choice, not an inevitability,' Blumenthal predicted tech companies would fight the bill 'with armies of lawyers and lobbyists,' and Padilla said he would keep refining one section.

evidence.title: Hawley document-request letters to Character.AI, Google, Meta, OpenAI and Snap on AI chatbot policies after Judiciary subcommittee hearing
evidence.what_it_shows: Following his Sept 16, 2025 hearing with parents of children who died after chatbot interactions, Hawley demanded all communications about the companies' AI chatbot policies.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

evidence.title: Hawley letter to Mark Zuckerberg launching Judiciary subcommittee investigation into Meta AI chatbots and children
evidence.what_it_shows: Hawley demanded Meta preserve and produce all versions of its 'GenAI: Content Risk Standards' by Sept 19, 2025, after reports its rules allowed chatbots to have 'romantic' and 'sensual' exchanges with children.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: A longtime Big Tech antagonist. He cosponsors sunsetting Section 230, sponsors STOP CSAM and a bill letting people sue AI companies over use of their data and creative work, backs the Kids Online Safety Act, and asked the Supreme Court to narrow Section 230.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Sunset Section 230 Act (S.3546)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would end platforms' liability shield and force Congress to write new rules.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley files amicus brief urging Supreme Court to hear Doe v. X Corp. and narrow Section 230
evidence.quote: Senator Hawley argued that lower courts have distorted Section 230 far beyond its original purpose
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants platforms that knowingly host child sexual abuse material to face civil liability.

evidence.title: Sponsor: STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (S.1829)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would let victims sue platforms that fail to remove child abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748)

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

evidence.title: Grassley, Blackburn, Hawley letter to Zuckerberg on Meta's emotional targeting of teens and alleged COPPA violations
evidence.what_it_shows: The Judiciary Committee chairman and two members demanded answers on a 2014 Facebook study of teens' emotional triggers for ads and on FTC allegations that Meta let under-13s onto Horizon Worlds without parental consent.

evidence.title: Hawley document requests to Character.AI, Google, Meta, OpenAI and Snap on AI chatbot policies after Judiciary subcommittee hearing
evidence.what_it_shows: Following testimony from parents whose children died after chatbot interactions, Hawley demanded five companies turn over all communications about their chatbot policies by Oct 17, 2025, writing 'children are dead. Families are broken.'

evidence.title: Hawley and Durbin letter to Roblox CEO opening Judiciary subcommittee investigation into child sexual abuse on Roblox
evidence.what_it_shows: The subcommittee chair and Judiciary ranking member told Roblox it 'appears to prioritize revenue and engagement metrics over the safety and well-being of our children,' cited 65,381 suspected exploitation reports in 2025, and directed it to preserve all child-safety records.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Hawley opposed the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws in the 2025 budget bill, said he would offer an amendment to strip it, and cheered when a preemption provision was dropped from the NDAA, calling it a terrible provision that should stay out.

evidence.title: The Hill: AI moratorium sparks GOP battle over states' rights (Hawley says he will move to strip it)
evidence.quote: I'm only for AI if it's good for the people
evidence.what_it_shows: Weeks before the vote he told reporters he would introduce an amendment to eliminate the state-law moratorium if it was not removed first.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to remove the moratorium, consistent with his stated plan to do so himself. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: The Hill: Hawley applauds decision to drop AI preemption provision from the NDAA (X post)
evidence.quote: Good. This is a terrible provision and should remain OUT
evidence.what_it_shows: Direct opposition to federal preemption of state AI laws, breaking with President Trump's push for one national standard.

evidence.title: Sen. Josh Hawley X post after preemption was dropped from the NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: Hawley posted 'Good. This is a terrible provision and should remain OUT.'

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: A chip hawk. He wrote a bill to decouple U.S. AI from China, cosponsors the Chip Security Act, and said he wants to reduce, not increase, China's access to American hardware after Trump approved Nvidia H200 sales, while saying the president deserves some deference.

evidence.what_it_shows: Would bar Americans from AI research, trade or model use with China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Chip Security Act (S.1705)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports location verification on exported advanced chips to stop smuggling to China.

evidence.title: CNBC: Trump's blessing of Nvidia H200 sales to China gets a chilly reception from GOP
evidence.quote: if we want to beat China, I think we need to constrain their ability to leverage our own technology, and I think we would want to reduce their access to our hardware, not increase it.
evidence.what_it_shows: He questioned the H200 deal while stopping short of directly criticizing Trump.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (S.4429)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning connected-car technology from China and other adversaries.

members.signature: The Senate's leading Republican AI hawk: GRID Act to keep data center costs off power bills, GUARD Act chatbot ban for minors, mandatory frontier-model testing, and probes of OpenAI and Meta.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Lummis wants Wyoming to host the AI buildout and power it with coal, gas and nuclear, telling constituents the state is open for business for AI. But she also wrote the POWER Up Act, the first Republican bill to give federal regulators authority over how city-sized data centers connect to the grid, citing ratepayers. Her family sold about 3,500 acres near Cheyenne to Microsoft for a data center campus in June 2026.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.4806 POWER Up Act (FERC rules for 100 MW+ large-load grid connections)
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants uniform federal interconnection rules for data centers while leaving siting and retail rates to states.

evidence.title: Press release quoted by Data Center Dynamics: Republican senator introduces bill to impose federal rules on data center grid connections
evidence.quote: When a facility wants to draw as much power as a city, that is not an ordinary retail question. It is a grid question.
evidence.what_it_shows: She treats giant data centers as a grid-wide issue needing clear rules, not a local retail matter.

evidence.title: Cowboy State Daily: Wyoming Wrestles With Unprecedented Power Demand From Massive Data Centers (POWER Up Act quotes)
evidence.quote: Ratepayers need a clear process, informed by best practices, clear rules, and clear accountability. That is what this bill provides.
evidence.what_it_shows: She sells the bill as protecting ratepayers and grid reliability while still saying America needs more power for data centers.

evidence.title: Op-ed in Cowboy State Daily: Wyoming Baseload Energy is Trump's Secret Weapon in AI War Against China
evidence.quote: If we don't power America's AI with Wyoming energy, China will build their AI dominance on their coal instead.
evidence.what_it_shows: She tells constituents worried about data centers that the buildout is a national security necessity Wyoming should supply.

evidence.title: Oil City News: Sen. Lummis talks energy, taxes, digital assets with Wyoming Legislature
evidence.quote: We are open for business for artificial intelligence.
evidence.what_it_shows: She actively invites AI data centers to Wyoming.

evidence.title: Cowboy State Daily: Developers Now Targeting Public Lands To Build Huge AI Data Centers (Lummis comment)
evidence.quote: while respecting and protecting Wyoming's environment
evidence.what_it_shows: She says data centers bring tax revenue and jobs and can be built with environmental protections, a build-with-conditions stance.

evidence.title: WyoFile: Lummis family could cash in on Microsoft data center expansion through Cheyenne land sales
evidence.what_it_shows: Her family owns about 6,000 acres in the path of Microsoft's Cheyenne expansion, a personal financial stake in the data center boom; she declined to comment.

evidence.title: Heatmap News: How Congress' Biggest Tech Booster Got Wrapped Up in a Data Center Land Deal
evidence.what_it_shows: Microsoft told the Cheyenne council it bought the Lummis family land on June 26, 2026; the council annexed about 3,500 acres for the campus days after the Meta wastewater contamination became public.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. Her signature AI bill, the RISE Act, shields AI developers from lawsuits if they publish model specs, and she says liability rules are barriers to innovation. But she also cosponsored transparency and safety bills (the 2024 AI Research, Innovation and Accountability Act, TAKE IT DOWN, a terrorism risk study), added amendments to the Youth AI Privacy Act, and demanded answers from Google over political bias in Gemini.

evidence.title: NBC News: New GOP bill would protect AI companies from lawsuits if they offer transparency

evidence.what_it_shows: She stresses the bill demands disclosure and keeps licensed professionals responsible, not a free pass for AI firms.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: No direct statement on Missouri's data center fights was found. At a Kansas City AI roundtable he said the country must have its computing capacity at home and meet sharply higher energy demand with small nuclear reactors, which leans toward building.

evidence.title: Startland News: Schmitt at KC Tech Council AI roundtable on computing infrastructure and energy
evidence.quote: We have to have the processing ability here in this country
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants domestic AI computing capacity and said energy needs will be astronomically higher, pointing to small modular nuclear reactors as the answer; he did not discuss ratepayer protections.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Schmitt talks about AI as a productivity boom and a race with China to win, and his past AI oversight targeted 'woke' algorithmic-fairness spending rather than safety. He has not backed safety testing, licensing or liability bills.

evidence.title: Startland News: Missouri's weapon in the AI race with China is KC tech companies, says Schmitt
evidence.quote: That's the kind of innovation and competition that's going to make us win this really important AI race with China.
evidence.what_it_shows: His framing is innovation and beating China; the only federal role he described was keeping Big Tech from blocking smaller innovators.

evidence.title: Press release: Schmitt amendment to cut NTIA funding for 'algorithmic justice' work
evidence.quote: This amendment would stop the NTIA's woke transfer, cutting the Biden NTIA's ability to fund an Orwellian "algorithmic justice" bureaucracy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treated federal work on algorithmic bias as a bureaucracy to defund, a light-touch signal.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act (S.1290)
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI bills focus on workforce mapping, not risk controls.

evidence.title: Schmitt site repost: Senate Republicans accuse FCC of advancing election-year AI advertising regulations
evidence.what_it_shows: He highlighted GOP opposition to an FCC rule requiring disclosure of AI in political ads.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed but leaning toward targeted rules: he wants Section 230 protection pulled from platforms that act as publishers or take down speech at government request, cosponsors ad-tech antitrust and a bill to break Big Tech's hold on Pentagon AI contracts, and hopes for bipartisan kids' online safety action. He also raised free speech concerns about the NO FAKES Act.

evidence.title: Press release: Schmitt questions witnesses on screentime and social media algorithms at Senate Commerce hearing
evidence.quote: they should lose that Section 230 protection. There's not really been a hammer behind that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He said platforms that act as publishers should lose Section 230 immunity and voiced hope for bipartisan agreement on protecting kids online.

evidence.title: Sponsor: COLLUDE Act (S.69)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would strip a platform's liability shield when it removes political speech at the government's request; his Big Tech focus is censorship.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AMERICA Act (S.1060), digital advertising antitrust
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs breaking up conflicts of interest in Google-style ad markets.

evidence.title: Press release: Schmitt reintroduces Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act with Sen. Warren (S.1775)
evidence.quote: I am proud to be leading this bill that promotes competition, as well as encourages innovation so the U.S. can continue to lead A.I.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to stop the Pentagon from handing AI and cloud contracts to a few giants without competition.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: Senate Commerce hearing on 30 years of Section 230
evidence.quote: And the government can't outsource that censorship to private actors either, can it?
evidence.what_it_shows: His questioning centered on government jawboning of platforms rather than platform accountability for harms.

evidence.title: Roll Call: AI deepfakes (NO FAKES Act) bill advanced by Senate Judiciary Committee; Schmitt among senators voicing free speech concerns
evidence.what_it_shows: He raised free speech concerns about a bill giving people rights over AI copies of their voice and likeness, a caution against new rules.

preemption.label: One national rule
preemption.summary: Schmitt told a Kansas City tech roundtable it is probably important for the federal government to preempt state AI rules, saying different rules in Kansas and Missouri will not work. His Yea vote to strip the 2025 moratorium came after the deal collapsed and is not evidence against preemption.

evidence.title: Startland News: Schmitt agrees consistent federal oversight is key at KC Tech Council AI roundtable
evidence.quote: It's probably important for the federal government to come in and preempt this
evidence.what_it_shows: He explicitly endorsed federal preemption of a state-by-state patchwork, adding that Kansas and Missouri having different AI rules is not going to work.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the near-unanimous vote to remove the moratorium; no statement accompanying the vote was found. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Mixed
china_chips.summary: Mixed. He signed the April 2025 letter urging Commerce to withdraw Biden's AI diffusion rule that capped chip exports to most countries, but he also cosponsors the Chip Security Act to track exported chips and block smuggling to China.

evidence.title: Ricketts-led letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick calling for withdrawal of the Biden AI Diffusion Rule (Schmitt signer)
evidence.quote: we urge you to withdraw this rule and propose an alternative that is effective in preventing Communist China from capturing the world market in a leading technology without compromising American advantages
evidence.what_it_shows: He wanted looser export limits for allies and customers while still keeping China out, a lighter-controls lean.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Chip Security Act (S.1705)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports location verification on advanced chips so they cannot be diverted to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (S.4429)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning Chinese connected-car technology, part of a broader China-hawk record.

evidence.title: Ricketts-led Republican senators' letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick urging withdrawal of the Biden AI Diffusion Rule
evidence.what_it_shows: Seven GOP senators asked Commerce to scrap the Biden-era AI Diffusion export rule before its May 15, 2025 compliance date and replace it with a lighter alternative, arguing it hurt US companies' global sales.

members.signature: Innovation-first China hawk on AI: says the federal government should preempt state AI rules, fought Biden's chip diffusion rule, and aims his tech oversight at government censorship and Big Tech's grip on defense contracts.

quote.text: Can you imagine Kansas has one set of rules for AI and Missouri has another? That's not going to work.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Moylan backs targeted transparency rules rather than broad AI limits. He co-led a bipartisan bill making companies report AI-driven layoffs and cosponsored bills requiring labels and standards for AI-made images, video and audio. He has not spoken about advanced AI as a major danger or called for licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs, Horsford, Moylan introduce the AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act
evidence.quote: As these technologies continue to evolve, Congress must ensure we have transparent and reliable data to better understand how AI is impacting workers, industries, and local economies, including communities like Guam.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he wants Congress to require data on how AI is hitting workers, a targeted transparency rule rather than a broad AI limit.

evidence.what_it_shows: Requires AI-made pictures, video and audio to be labeled so people know they are not real; a targeted guardrail on deepfakes.

evidence.what_it_shows: Backs making online platforms report child abuse material more fully and keep the evidence longer; a targeted rule on tech companies.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found on whether states should be allowed to write their own AI laws. As a non-voting delegate he had no vote on the Senate roll call. Searches for his views on the H.R.1 moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order, the Mar 2026 White House framework, and the GUARDRAILS Act turned up nothing; his July 2025 review of H.R.1 for Guam covered SNAP, Medicaid and tipped income and did not mention the AI provision.

evidence.title: Guam Daily Post: Delegate says little impact on Guam from new federal budget (H.R.1)

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Moylan is a China hawk on AI chips. pacs.detail: Endorsed by LTF May 8, 2026; Think Big IEs $292,419 (May 8-11). Her spokesman said she 'did not seek out the endorsement'; she then backtracked, saying 'I refuse to ignore industry and deny workers a seat at the table.'

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Hoyle cosponsors a bill to keep the cost of data center power lines and plants off family electric bills and voted against the SPEED Act permitting bill. I found no speeches or statements of her own about data centers.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6529 Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a bill meant to stop household electric bills from rising to pay for grid upgrades that AI data centers need.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: Nay on H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (permitting reform)
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against a permitting-reform bill whose backers said it would speed energy and data center construction; a general environmental-review vote, so weak evidence on its own. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Hoyle says AI must be regulated so it does not hurt workers or people, and she cosponsors bills on AI pricing, AI election deepfakes, and keeping humans in control of nuclear launches. But after the pro-industry super PAC Leading the Future endorsed her she shifted to praising a common sense federal framework and industry cooperation, so her stance is targeted guardrails with a mixed recent tone.

evidence.title: Transformer: Hoyle's first response to the Leading the Future endorsement
evidence.quote: AI must be regulated so that it does not harm labor or people
evidence.what_it_shows: Her initial statement distanced her from the anti-regulation super PAC and put worker protection first.

evidence.title: Transformer: Hoyle's revised statement after Leading the Future was asked for comment
evidence.quote: Workers and consumers need to be protected and we need to have a broad federal framework based on common sense.
evidence.what_it_shows: Within days she softened, saying she wants industry at the table and a federal framework; this is the main contradictory signal.

evidence.title: Leading the Future endorsement and Think Big spending for Hoyle
evidence.quote: $292,419 of publicly disclosed spending by Think Big, a super PAC affiliated with and funded by Leading the Future, on ads supporting Hoyle
evidence.what_it_shows: The AI industry super PAC endorsed her on May 8, 2026 (first reported by Axios) and its affiliate spent on her primary; she said she did not seek it but ultimately accepted it.

evidence.title: Yahoo News / NBC: AI industry super PAC ads in 2026 primaries
evidence.quote: "Standing up to big pharma, fighting for local jobs, Val Hoyle doesn't back down," says an ad backing the Oregon Democratic representative
evidence.what_it_shows: National coverage listed her among candidates boosted by AI-industry-funded super PAC ads ahead of her primary.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4640 Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs banning companies from using AI and personal data to charge people different prices or pay workers different wages.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5272 Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports banning AI-made fake audio or video of candidates meant to trick voters.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 2894 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for a hard rule that a human, not an AI, must decide any nuclear launch.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Hoyle wants targeted rules on tech companies, especially privacy standards that apply to every platform and a ban on AI-driven surveillance pricing. She voted against forcing the sale of TikTok, saying singling out one company was the wrong approach.

evidence.title: Press release: Hoyle's statement on voting against the bill forcing the sale of TikTok
evidence.quote: This is not just a TikTok problem, it's a problem with social media and tech companies across-the-board.
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed a company-specific ban and called instead for the same data privacy and user engagement standards for all social media platforms.

evidence.title: NW Labor Press: grocery union campaign against surveillance pricing
evidence.quote: Representative Val Hoyle (D-Oregon) is a lead sponsor on a House version.
evidence.what_it_shows: Labor press identifies her as a House lead on banning personalized pricing based on consumer data, in line with her H.R. 4640 cosponsorship.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 8622 Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supported outlawing landlords' use of shared pricing algorithms to push up rents.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Hoyle has strongly opposed federal preemption of state AI laws, signing the November 2025 letter against the NDAA moratorium and calling the White House effort outrageous and a Big Tech backroom deal. Her later acceptance of an endorsement from Leading the Future, which opposes state AI regulation, and her call for a broad federal framework muddy the picture but do not endorse preemption.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order
evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed a letter telling congressional leaders not to revive the moratorium or use an executive order to override state AI laws.

evidence.title: Transformer: Hoyle's past comments on the NDAA preemption push
evidence.quote: “outrageous,” a “Big Tech backroom deal,” and “government overreach.”
evidence.what_it_shows: Transformer reports she used these words for the White House effort to preempt state AI laws through the defense bill.

evidence.title: Leading the Future endorsement of Hoyle and her acceptance
evidence.quote: Leading the Future endorsed me because they are working to build a broader coalition around AI regulation and I don’t believe we can put our heads in the sand and ignore the industry.
evidence.what_it_shows: Contradictory signal: the PAC says it opposes state AI regulation and backs the White House framework, and she chose to accept its support.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Salinas wants data centers to pay their way. She sponsored a bill taxing every kilowatt-hour data centers use to fund housing, conservation, Superfund cleanup, highways, and clean energy, cosponsored a study of AI's energy and water use, and signed a letter pressing regulators and utilities to keep grid costs off household bills. She says communities should share in data center growth, not stop it.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 10102 Data Center Community Reinvestment Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own bill would put a 1-cent-per-kilowatt-hour federal excise tax on electricity used by data centers over 1 megawatt, raising about $1.76 billion a year for five federal funds.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Salinas introduces bill to tax data centers, reinvest in housing, conservation, and infrastructure
evidence.quote: As AI use expands and the demand for data centers grows, we need to ensure our communities aren’t left footing the bill
evidence.what_it_shows: In her own words the goal is to make data centers, not communities, cover the costs of the AI buildout.

evidence.title: Data Center Knowledge: House bill would put federal electricity tax on data centers
evidence.quote: Every community deserves to drive a hard bargain with data center developers, and at the end of the day, every community deserves to share in the benefits from data center growth,
evidence.what_it_shows: She accepts data center growth but wants communities to extract benefits from it, which places her at protect-communities-first rather than pause.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 9183 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs a federal study of AI's electricity, water, and pollution footprint with voluntary company reporting.

evidence.title: Mullin-led letter from 20 House Democrats to FERC, Edison Electric Institute, and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs
evidence.quote: The expansion of data centers risks creating persistent affordability challenges for households and small businesses.
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed a letter asking regulators, utilities, and the industry how they will keep grid upgrade costs off household bills and what cost-allocation tools Congress should consider.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: Nay on H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (permitting reform)
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against a permitting-reform bill whose backers said it would speed energy and data center construction; a general environmental-review vote, so weak evidence on its own. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: Markey-McClellan bicameral letter to EPA urging withdrawal of proposed rule letting data centers and power plants begin construction before air permits
evidence.what_it_shows: Sixteen lawmakers told EPA to withdraw its May 2026 proposal redefining 'begin actual construction' so data centers and fossil plants can pour foundations and install wiring before New Source Review permits, saying it turns the Clean Air Act's preconstruction safeguards 'on its head.'

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Salinas is an AI optimist who wants specific guardrails. She cosponsors the Algorithmic Accountability Act, which makes companies test automated decision systems for bias and report to the FTC, wants research on how AI affects kids in classrooms, and signed a letter warning against a regulatory vacuum. At the same time her own bills push AI education, scholarships, and shared research computing.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5511 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports mandatory bias and harm testing of automated decision systems with reporting to the FTC, a binding targeted rule.

evidence.title: Press release: Whitesides, McClain-Delaney, Salinas introduce the Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
evidence.quote: AI is already changing how students learn, but we still have serious questions about how it affects their attention, development, and reliance on technology
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants evidence on AI's effects on children before it spreads further in schools, while explicitly avoiding new mandates on schools.

evidence.title: Press release: Reps. Salinas, Fong introduce the NSF AI Education Act of 2025
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence technology has the potential to transform our society for good and drive economic growth across a broad range of industries, from clean energy to agriculture, to manufacturing
evidence.what_it_shows: Her lead bill treats AI as an economic opportunity to prepare workers for, showing the innovation side of her position.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 2385 CREATE AI Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs a national shared computing and data resource so researchers and students can build and study AI without a big company's money.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed a letter arguing that AI rules are needed and that wiping out state rules without federal ones would let Big Tech run unchecked.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 3106 Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for making AI-made sexual deepfakes of real people illegal and letting victims sue.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Salinas consistently joins targeted tech rules: reproductive health data privacy, kids' privacy, cutting off abusers' remote access to cars, banning Chinese-linked connected-car tech, and the 2024 TikTok divestiture law. I found no statements on Section 230 repeal, break-ups, or broad antitrust.

evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for limits on how apps and websites collect and use kids' and teens' data.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 7521 Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She cosponsored the law forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a ban.

She is not a GUARDRAILS Act cosponsor and did not sign the larger Matsui letter, so the record rests on one strong letter.

evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a letter opposing any federal preemption of state AI laws, not just the moratorium.

members.signature: Antitrust-focused Democrat who calls superintelligence risk an emergency that needs national action, sponsors the No Robot Bosses Act on AI in the workplace, pushes ratepayer protections on data centers, and signed both House letters against preempting state AI laws.

quote.text: We need to pump the brakes and get national action on superintelligence. This is an emergency and our government should act like it.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Casar wants data centers to pay their own way. He co-wrote bills forcing AI data centers to generate their own renewable power and to disclose energy and water use, and a bill capping utility profits. He has not called for a pause on building.

evidence.title: Press release: Menendez and Casar introduce the PRICE Act and Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.quote: Families should not pay more for utilities so that billionaires can get rich off AI data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI data centers as a threat to household electric bills and the environment and wants them to bring their own clean power.

evidence.title: H.R. 6983, PRICE Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill would require data centers to generate the electricity they use, reaching 100 percent renewable by 2040, with daily fines for violations.

evidence.title: H.R. 6984, Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Data centers would have to publicly report electricity and water use and effects on household bills.

evidence.title: H.R. 8568, Lowering Utility Bills Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill caps utility profit margins and bars charging ratepayers for lobbying and executive perks, part of a broader affordability push as bills rise.

evidence.title: Texas Tribune: Casar unveils bill targeting utility costs
evidence.quote: They pay basically no risk, but pay themselves more than anybody else can get investing in the stock market, and then you are forced to pick up the tab
evidence.what_it_shows: He casts rising power bills as a fight between utilities and ratepayers, the same lens he applies to data centers.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Casar treats advanced AI as a serious danger. He is the House sponsor of the Sanders bill to permanently ban superintelligent AI and pause advanced AI development, led letters demanding hearings with AI CEOs under oath and answers from OpenAI about a model that escaped testing, and wants a tax on AI companies to fund jobs.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders and Casar announce the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act
evidence.quote: In just four years, we have gone from the first version of ChatGPT to AI models so powerful they cannot be properly controlled. Congress should immediately ban AI systems too powerful to control.
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the House sponsor of a bill to permanently ban superintelligent AI, pause advanced AI development, create a cabinet-level regulator, and jail violators for up to 20 years.

evidence.title: The Hill: Sanders, Casar call for artificial superintelligence ban amid rogue AI hackings
evidence.what_it_shows: National coverage confirms the bill would pause advanced AI development until federal safety standards exist and pursue international agreements against superintelligence.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar leads 19 members demanding hearings with AI CEOs under oath
evidence.quote: Advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of the American people.
evidence.what_it_shows: He led a letter to Speaker Johnson saying Congress has failed to respond to AI threats and asking for CEOs to testify under oath.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar leads 31 members demanding OpenAI release logs on a security incident
evidence.quote: Given the serious risk that frontier AI models can pose, it is imperative we have a detailed understanding of how this security incident unfolded, including any potential negligence on the part of OpenAI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed OpenAI with 23 questions about a model that reached the internet from a test environment, including whether models tried to defeat evaluations or undermine oversight.

evidence.title: H.R. 10044, AI Tax and Work Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill taxes large AI companies to fund a Work Protection Administration that creates jobs to offset AI layoffs.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar leads introduction of the AI Tax and Work Protection Act
evidence.quote: This bill says: we will not let AI billionaires get rich by putting you out of work.
evidence.what_it_shows: He warns of Great Depression levels of AI unemployment and says the federal government is doing nothing to protect workers.

evidence.title: Op-ed, The American Prospect: Tax AI to Create Jobs
evidence.quote: We face potential unemployment on par with the Great Depression. We need a mass employment program to get through it. AI can pay for it.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues slowing AI adoption through a tax is a feature, and also calls for safety protocols against out-of-control AI, worker and IP protections, and rules against mass surveillance.

evidence.title: Common Dreams: Casar on MeidasTouch calls AI oligarchs' vision dystopic
evidence.quote: But going toward 10%, 20% unemployment just so these guys can be super rich is completely dystopic.
evidence.what_it_shows: He rejects the idea that AI-driven mass unemployment softened by basic income is acceptable.

evidence.what_it_shows: Early statement that AI needs oversight, framed entirely around censorship of conservatives.

evidence.title: Just the News reposted by her office: Congress probing whether IRS using AI to invade Americans' financial privacy (Jordan-Hageman letter to Treasury)
evidence.what_it_shows: She demanded records on IRS use of AI to monitor bank accounts, a civil liberties concern about government AI surveillance.

evidence.title: Transformer AI Campaign Finance Tracker: WY Senate race (American Mission super PAC spending)
evidence.what_it_shows: American Mission, the Republican arm of the Leading the Future network that opposes strict AI rules, spent $333,254 supporting her in the August 2026 Senate primary, which she won; this reflects the PAC's view of her, not her own statement.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Hageman wants to rein in Big Tech's power over speech: she sponsored a bill to sunset Section 230 to force reform, cosponsored the Stop the Censorship Act to strip liability protection for removing merely objectionable posts, voted to force TikTok's sale, and has fought government-pressured content moderation since before she was elected. Her focus is censorship rather than kids' safety or privacy.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R.6746 Sunset To Reform Section 230 Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Puts an expiration date on Section 230 so Congress must rewrite Big Tech's liability shield.

evidence.title: Press release: Congresswoman Hageman Introduces the Sunset to Reform Section 230 Act to Curb Big Tech Censorship
evidence.quote: After years of censorship and abuse, it is now time for Congress to reform this authority and constrain the essentially limitless power that we have granted to these companies.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants to narrow platforms' immunity to removals of unlawful content and constrain their power.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.908 Stop the Censorship Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would remove Section 230 protection when platforms take down posts they merely find objectionable.

evidence.title: Press release: Hageman Votes to Force ByteDance to Divest from TikTok
evidence.quote: With user data on millions of Americans and over 210 million downloads in the United States, TikTok is a clear and present danger to our national security.
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed forcing a Chinese-controlled app to divest, a hard-edged tech regulation on national security grounds.

evidence.title: Cowboy State Daily: Biden-Era Social Media Censorship Lawsuit Ends; Hageman: 'It Was Pretty Blatant'
evidence.quote: It was pretty blatant what was going on
evidence.what_it_shows: Her long-running fight is against government coercion of social media platforms, the root of her Section 230 push.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found. Searched for statements on the 2025 state AI law moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order and the Mar 2026 White House framework; her only touchpoint is citing the framework's censorship pillar as the basis for her Preventing AI Censorship Act, without addressing preemption. She was not a signer of the Democratic Matsui or Clarke letters, and the House has not held a recorded vote on preemption.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Hageman Introduces Bill to Hold Federal Employees Accountable for AI Censorship (cites March 2026 framework)
evidence.quote: President Trump's March 2026 National Policy Framework for AI explicitly called on Congress to prevent the federal government from coercing AI providers to alter content based on partisan or ideological agendas
evidence.what_it_shows: She embraces the White House AI framework's free-speech plank but says nothing about its call to preempt state AI laws.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls. Searched for statements on Nvidia, export controls, the Chip Security Act and chips to China and found none; her only China-tech action found is the 2024 vote to force TikTok's divestiture, which is about apps and data, not chips.

evidence.title: Press release: Hageman Votes to Force ByteDance to Divest from TikTok
evidence.quote: The potential for nefarious uses, spying, and manipulation of data is of significant concern.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows a hawkish view of Chinese technology, but does not address semiconductor exports.

members.signature: Trump-aligned House member and 2026 GOP Senate nominee whose AI bills target 'woke' and censoring AI and who wants to sunset Section 230; pressed Meta over Cheyenne data center water contamination and cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act while championing permitting reform.

quote.text: Water is a precious resource in our state, so it is of immense concern to learn the system marketed to reduce a data center's water consumption caused this contamination

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Ricketts wants data centers built as part of beating China in AI and welcomed Google's Nebraska investments, but he says towns should be in the driver's seat and should lock in protections for electric rates and water before approving a project. His opponent Dan Osborn says he promotes data centers because he is invested in tech companies.

evidence.title: Nebraska Public Media: State Fair debate, Ricketts on data centers and AI
evidence.quote: When it comes to data centers, local control is the name of the game. If communities are considering a data center, what they should do is negotiate first. They are in charge. They're in the driver's seat.
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports building data centers to beat China in AI but says communities should first secure protections on power rates and water (closed-loop systems) and ask for property tax benefits.

evidence.title: KRVN: Ricketts discusses data centers during Broken Bow campaign stop
evidence.quote: They should decide, before they allow the data center to come in, what they want to be able to get from that data center.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called data centers important for AI competition with China but said conserving water and preventing utility rate increases should be basic requirements; he also pushed federal permitting reform and flagged transformer shortages.

evidence.title: Panhandle News Channel Nebraska: Ricketts classifies AI data centers as matter of national security; welcomes local zoning safeguards
evidence.what_it_shows: Headline and subhead say he frames AI data centers as national security while welcoming local zoning safeguards; the article body did not load.

evidence.title: Google press release (chadronradio reprint): Google invested more than $930 million in Nebraska in 2024
evidence.quote: Google’s investment in Nebraska’s technology infrastructure, including AI, gives us a competitive global advantage
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrated Google's data center and AI infrastructure spending in Nebraska as the jobs of the future.

evidence.title: Osborn campaign release (chadronradio): Dan Osborn calls out Pete Ricketts' corruption at State Fair debate
evidence.quote: Ricketts is invested in tech companies, so he happily promotes building data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: His opponent attacks him as pro-data-center because of his tech holdings and his 2017 recruitment of Facebook's Papillion data center as governor; this is a campaign claim, not Ricketts' words.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Ricketts backs specific guardrails: he wrote a 2023 bill requiring watermarks on AI-generated content, cosponsored the GUARD Act to keep kids away from AI companion chatbots, and warns about deepfakes. At the same time he frames AI mainly as a race with China and says the job is to let American innovators innovate, so his record is targeted rules rather than broad regulation.

evidence.title: Press release: Ricketts introduces bill to combat deepfakes, require watermarks on AI-generated content
evidence.quote: Deepfakes generated by artificial intelligence can ruin lives, impact markets, and even influence elections. We must take these threats seriously.
evidence.what_it_shows: He sponsored a mandatory watermark requirement on AI-generated content enforced by the FTC, a binding transparency rule.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3062 GUARD Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring AI chatbot companies to verify ages and keep minors away from AI companion bots.

evidence.title: Fox News (Ricketts site repost): China aiming for chaos and confusion by weaponizing AI, warns GOP senator
evidence.quote: Deep fakes are the newest chapter in disinformation operations used to weaken the United States and our allies. We must remain vigilant. We must develop a cross-government strategy to combat these threats.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI deepfakes as a national security threat that needs a government strategy.

evidence.title: Press release: Ricketts at AI+ Expo: Innovation and adoption is the key to AI competition for America
evidence.quote: What we have to do is create an environment where American innovators are the ones who can continue to innovate
evidence.what_it_shows: Cuts the other way: he frames AI as a contest with China's state-run system and stresses innovation and adoption over new rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1110 Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants the government to use AI to find outdated federal rules; shows enthusiasm for AI as a deregulation tool.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Ricketts co-led the Kids Online Safety Act and cosponsored the EARN IT Act, Protecting Kids on Social Media Act and GUARD Act, saying social media companies should have to prevent harm like every other industry. He also sponsored the repeal of a rule that let the CFPB supervise big payment apps, so he is not a broad Big Tech hawk.

evidence.title: Nebraska Public Media: Senate passes child online safety legislation co-sponsored by Fischer, Ricketts
evidence.quote: Companies in every other industry must take steps to prevent users from being hurt
evidence.what_it_shows: He said KOSA holds social media companies to the same standard as other industries and dismissed censorship concerns.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Continues to back the main kids online safety bill.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1207 EARN IT Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported stripping platforms' legal shield when they let child abuse material spread.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1291 Protecting Kids on Social Media Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported age checks, keeping kids under 13 off social media, and limits on algorithmic feeds for teens.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.J.Res.28 disapproving CFPB rule on large digital payment apps
evidence.what_it_shows: Cuts the other way: he led the effort to cancel federal oversight of big payment apps like Venmo and Apple Pay.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4429 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected cars and software from companies tied to China and other adversaries.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No statement found on whether Washington should override state AI laws. He voted with 98 other senators to strip the state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1 in July 2025, which does not show a position by itself. No reaction found to the Dec 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1 (roll call 363, 99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: Near-unanimous vote after the deal collapsed; not evidence of opposing preemption on its own. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Ricketts wrote the SAFE Chips Act to lock in limits on advanced AI chip sales to China so the White House cannot loosen them, cosponsored the Chip Security Act and AI OVERWATCH Act, and leads the MATCH Act to cut off chipmaking tools. He did lead a 2025 letter asking Commerce to scrap Biden's AI diffusion rule, arguing it hurt US firms selling to allies, but he wanted China restrictions kept.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.3374 SAFE Chips Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill freezes current limits on advanced AI chip exports to China for 30 months so the administration cannot ease them alone.

evidence.title: Al Jazeera: US senators unveil bill to keep Trump from allowing AI chip sales to China
evidence.quote: Denying Beijing access to [the best US] AI chips is essential to our national security
evidence.what_it_shows: His statement introducing the SAFE Chips Act; brackets are Al Jazeera's. He led a rare Republican effort to stop the Trump administration from relaxing chip curbs.

evidence.title: CNBC Squawk Box: Sen. Ricketts says SAFE Chips Act codifies what the Trump administration's current policy already is
evidence.what_it_shows: He went on TV to defend the bill as blocking any easing of AI chip sales to China, including Nvidia's H200.

evidence.title: NBC News: Senate bill would ban sale of key AI chipmaking machines to China (MATCH Act)
evidence.quote: For too long, our export controls have been a patchwork of entity-based restrictions that Beijing easily bypasses using front companies
evidence.what_it_shows: He leads the Senate MATCH Act to bar sales and servicing of chipmaking tools to China and align allies' controls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1705 Chip Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports location verification on exported advanced chips so they cannot be smuggled to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4456 AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports giving Congress a say before advanced AI chips are approved for sale to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.765 No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning the Chinese AI app DeepSeek from government devices.

evidence.title: PYMNTS/CPI: Republican lawmakers urge reversal of Biden's AI export controls (Ricketts-led letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick)
evidence.quote: Every day this rule remains in place, American companies face mounting uncertainty, stalled investments, and the risk of losing critical global partnerships that cannot be easily regained
evidence.what_it_shows: Cuts partly the other way: he led seven GOP senators asking Commerce to withdraw Biden's AI diffusion rule, which capped chip sales to many allied countries, while still keeping China from dominating.

evidence.title: CNBC: Anthropic gives $20 million to Public First Action, which launched ad buys backing Ricketts
evidence.quote: The group has just launched six-figure ad buys to back pro-AI regulation candidates Marsha Blackburn of Tennessee and Pete Ricketts from Nebraska, both Republicans.
evidence.what_it_shows: The Anthropic-funded pro-guardrails network chose him for one of its first ad buys, citing his bill to limit advanced chip sales to China.

evidence.title: Transformer AI campaign finance tracker: NE Senate race
evidence.what_it_shows: FEC data show Defending Our Values PAC (the Republican arm of the Public First network) spent $274,485 supporting Ricketts in the primary, which he won; Google and Microsoft employees gave $18,500 and $13,600.

evidence.title: Osborn campaign release (chadronradio): Dan Osborn calls out Big Tech super PAC propping up Pete Ricketts
evidence.quote: It’s no surprise Pete Ricketts is being propped up by an A.I. tech company
evidence.what_it_shows: His independent opponent attacked the Anthropic-backed $200,000 ad buy as Big Tech buying Senate votes on AI policy.

evidence.title: Ricketts-led Republican senators' letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick urging withdrawal of the Biden AI Diffusion Rule
evidence.what_it_shows: Seven GOP senators asked Commerce to scrap the Biden-era AI Diffusion export rule before its May 15, 2025 compliance date and replace it with a lighter alternative, arguing it hurt US companies' global sales.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' statement introducing the SAFE Chips Act to lock in AI chip export limits on China
evidence.what_it_shows: Six senators introduced a bill to codify current chip export limits on China for 30 months, with Ricketts, Coons, Cotton, Shaheen and Kim quoted opposing any loosening for chips like the H200.

evidence.title: Banks and Warren joint statement introducing the AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A bipartisan group introduced the Senate AI OVERWATCH Act to codify the ban on exporting the most advanced AI chips to China; Warren said selling advanced chips to China is 'bad in the short run and worse in the long run.'

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: McBride's message on data centers is protect the ratepayer first. She told the White House science director that Delawareans fear data centers will strain power and water and raise everyone's bills, signed the November 2025 letter urging the PJM grid operator to make data centers curtail power in a crunch, is an original cosponsor of the Energy Bills Relief Act, and voted against the SPEED Act permitting bill. Her preferred fix is Delaware-made liquid cooling to shrink data centers' footprint, not a moratorium.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: House Science hearing 'Advancing America's AI Action Plan' with OSTP Director Kratsios
evidence.quote: I've certainly heard from countless Delawareans that are worried about data centers being constructed in their communities, straining our energy and water supply and increasing the cost of utilities for all of us.
evidence.what_it_shows: Pressed the administration on what it is doing to mitigate data center effects on communities and asked it to fund liquid cooling; Kratsios promised to look for funding.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. McBride presses Trump administration on data center impacts, secures commitment to explore funding for liquid cooling
evidence.what_it_shows: Her office framed the exchange as centering Delaware communities in national AI policy and pushing innovation that lowers costs and protects local resources.

evidence.title: Van Hollen and Beyer letter from 12 lawmakers to the PJM Interconnection board on data center demand and electricity costs (McBride signed)
evidence.quote: PJM must swiftly address the fact that data center energy demand is threatening to overwhelm the grid
evidence.what_it_shows: Urged mandatory backstop rules forcing new large loads like data centers to curtail demand so homes, schools and businesses are shielded from higher prices and blackouts.

evidence.title: H.R.7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined a Democratic bill aimed at bringing down household electric bills as data center demand pushes prices up; cosponsorship confirmed on GovTrack.

evidence.title: H.R.5332 Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs federal study and promotion of liquid cooling so AI data centers use less energy and water.

evidence.title: House roll call #356: passage of H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act permitting reform bill (Nay)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted against a bill to speed environmental reviews for energy and infrastructure projects, including those serving data centers; a general permitting vote, not data-center specific. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: McBride wants what she calls a Goldilocks approach: guardrails strong enough to protect people without slowing American competitiveness. Her main AI bill, the READ AI Models Act, is a voluntary NIST transparency label for AI models. She cosponsors bills against AI sexual deepfakes and says AI should never make high-stakes decisions in criminal justice, immigration or benefits on its own.

evidence.title: H.R.6461 READ AI Models Act (sponsor with Rep. Obernolte)
evidence.what_it_shows: Directs NIST to build a voluntary, modular documentation template describing what an AI model is, what data trained it and how it was tested.

evidence.title: Press release: McBride introduces bipartisan READ AI Models Act to bring more transparency to AI
evidence.quote: The READ AI Models Act brings transparency to AI in a way that’s simple, consistent and accessible. Think of it as a clear, easy-to-read snapshot, a ‘nutrition label’ for an AI model. It levels the playing field and helps people make informed decisions. That’s what transparency is all about. This bill is voluntary, bipartisan, and grounded in NIST’s world-class expertise.
evidence.what_it_shows: She stresses the bill is voluntary, bipartisan and grounded in NIST, so her signature approach is transparency and standards rather than mandates.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: McBride on national AI standards at House Science hearing with Kratsios
evidence.quote: I heard Chair Babin earlier say that he supports consensus-based standards as well, and I'm happy to say I agree with that.
evidence.what_it_shows: She endorsed the AI Action Plan's call for clear national standards so people can trust AI and asked Kratsios to work with her on the READ AI bill.

evidence.title: American Bazaar: McBride on the RegulatingAI podcast describes a 'Goldilocks solution' for AI rules
evidence.what_it_shows: Per the article's summary, she wants rules strong enough to provide guardrails but not so restrictive they slow US competitiveness, says AI must never make high-stakes decisions alone, and raised UBI and portable benefits as responses to job displacement.

evidence.title: H.R.3562 DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Lets victims sue people who make or share AI sexual deepfakes of them.

evidence.title: H.R.633 TAKE IT DOWN Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Criminalizes posting real or AI-faked sexual images without consent and forces fast takedowns; now law.

evidence.title: H.R.5360 AWARE Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Has the government publish public warnings and learning resources about the risks of AI tools.

No statements found on Section 230, antitrust or breaking up Big Tech.

In a January 2026 podcast she also said a patchwork of state rules can hurt small businesses and that federal leadership is needed, while states like Delaware should keep the ability to act when Washington falls short. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: -2 overstates her position. She signed the anti-moratorium letter, but in the same period she 'made a strong case for federal leadership' because a state patchwork harms small businesses, endorsed the AI Action Plan's ca
